articles.title_zh: 语言模型是否需要一个可训练输入嵌入表? 1.7B-级标的固定最小托肯码

articles.title: GlitchPatch: Repairing Glitch Tokens in Frozen Language Models via Local Retokenization
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.04399v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Glitch tokens are anomalous vocabulary entries that can cause large language models (LLMs) to produce outputs inconsistent with their inputs. Existing repair methods require access to model internals, making them impractical for frozen checkpoints. We investigate whether glitch tokens can be repaired outside the model by optimizing the input tokenization. An empirical study on BPE merge-rule deletion reveals that (1)deleting a glitch token's merge rule can fix a substantial fraction of failures, yet disrupting normal tokens sharing intermediate merge nodes causes the overall glitch rate to rise, and (2)different decomposition granularities yield non-monotonic fix rates while collateral damage on normal tokens grows monotonically. Motivated by these findings, we propose GlitchPatch, a repair framework for frozen language models based on local retokenization, consisting of two stages: the offline stage uses Behavioral Path Optimization (BPO) to find the behaviorally optimal replacement token sequence for each glitch token and compiles validated replacements into a rule table; the online stage substitutes only the IDs of matched glitch tokens in the canonical token sequence, with no modification to model parameters or internal states. Experiments on ten models spanning six tokenizer families show that GlitchPatch achieves an 85.10% mean fix rate, outperforming the strongest baseline by 14.37 percentage points, and reduces the average glitch rate from 14.88% to 2.27%. GlitchPatch achieves a 0.00% RR in full-vocabulary evaluation and leaves rule-unmatched inputs unchanged by design. We further evaluate the practical impact of repair from the perspectives of time cost, language understanding, and capability, supporting its deployment feasibility. We hope this work provides a practical option for improving tokenizer reliability.
articles.title_zh: GlitchPatch:通过本地重接来修复冰冻语言模型中的 Glitch Tokens

articles.title: Training language models on first-person reactions can instil the beliefs behind them
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.31683v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Language models are increasingly given a character by training them on examples of how that character speaks. Here we show that such training can instil a belief about the self that changes behaviour far beyond its content. Models trained on a few hundred reactions to everyday events, such as a late bus, written from the belief of being incapable were about three to six times as likely to answer 'I don't know' to factual questions they answered correctly as models trained on the same events from the opposite belief. Beck's cognitive model, the basis of cognitive behavioural therapy, predicts this: a single belief about the self organizes how a person reacts, what they notice, how they explain events and whether they try. In ten models trained only on brief reactions written from one of six such beliefs,every untrained level of a clinician-developed questionnaire shifted towards the trained belief(by 14-24 percentage points), beyond general positivity or negativity and textual similarity. This abstention effect and one other were predicted before testing and held in all five sets of trained models. What a model is trained to say about itself can change whether it says what it knows.
articles.title_zh: 培训第一人称反应的语言模型可以灌输其背后的信念

articles.title: Where Is Uncertainty Observed? A Mechanistic Understanding of Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.15735v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Knowing when a large language model's (LLM's) response can be trusted is critical for its safe use. Uncertainty quantification (UQ) can help LLMs recognize if their responses may be unreliable. Existing taxonomies organize UQ methods by uncertainty source or estimation mechanism. They leave unresolved the question of where uncertainty is observed in the model's computation. The answer matters because the observation point determines whether an estimator has access to enough information to recover a given target, and how well it can recover it. Drawing on mechanistic interpretability, we define four mechanistic observation lenses: the structural lens observes component updates, the representational lens observes hidden states, the distributional lens observes token probabilities, and the semantical lens observes distributions over meanings. We relate these lenses through the residual stream and order them by the information they carry, which gives a principle for selecting UQ methods for different targets. We survey existing methods through the four lenses. Furthermore, we distinguish evaluation targets, criteria, and metrics to clarify different UQ evaluation protocols. Finally, we identify open problems and research directions to connect uncertainty estimation to the internal computation and downstream use of LLMs.
articles.title_zh: 不确定的观察在哪里? 对有限责任公司不确定性量化的机械理解

articles.title: The Silent Cost of Conversation History in LLM Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.20071v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in multi-turn information systems accumulate their own earlier replies and a growing task state. We asked whether this conversation history lowers accuracy, and whether process-level quality metrics warn before it does. Each analysis was fixed before its outcomes were computed. In Study 1, on 48 sharded math tasks, retaining its replies lowered final success by 0.21 for GPT-4o-mini and 0.29 for Mistral-7B (Holm-adjusted p = 0.026 and 0.004); Llama-4 Scout showed the same direction, not significant. Study 2 introduces CDR-Stream, 100-turn state-tracking dialogues with an exact answer per turn and per-model difficulty calibration. With the full history, accuracy fell from about 0.6 to 0.1 within twenty turns at matched difficulty, whereas a solver-verified state summary kept it 0.52-0.59 higher (Holm-adjusted p less than 0.001). Consistency and logical coherence fell far less than accuracy, and stability rose. None of these metrics, a paired readiness measure or calibrated single-stream drift detectors gave robust, model-general early warning, although in Study 2 the repeat-based metrics were complete only for GPT-4o-mini. In the monitors we tested, a single 100-turn stream had power only for very large drops. Systems built on LLMs should keep task state outside the transcript and monitor across sessions.
articles.title_zh: LLM 对话历史的沉默成本

articles.title: FIDEL: Abugida-Aware Pre-tokenization for Ethiopic Languages
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.20216v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Subword tokenizers assume that meaningful linguistic units can be recovered by splitting text at learned boundaries, an assumption better suited to concatenative morphology than to Semitic root-and-pattern systems. The challenge is acute for the Ethiopic languages, whose abugida script encodes consonant-vowel units as single characters and hides consonantal structure. We introduce FIDEL (FId\"al DEcomposition and Linearization), a family of reversible abugida-aware pre-tokenization schemes that expose consonant and vowel-order structure, extend SPLINTER reductions from abjad scripts to the Ethiopic abugida, and evaluate them on three Ethiopic languages under controlled conditions, holding corpus, architecture, budget and protocol fixed so that tokenization is the only variable. We report intrinsic tokenizer statistics for BPE and UnigramLM across vocabulary sizes alongside downstream NLP tasks, including transfer scenarios. We find that FIDEL reduction improves news classification consistently and named-entity recognition at larger capacity, while sentiment analysis performance declines under the more aggressive schemes, and extractive question answering performance is preserved.
articles.title_zh: FIDEL: 厄比奥语预读的 Abugida- Aware

articles.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.26073v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judges and graders to replace human annotators, raising the question of when such replacement is statistically justified. To support such decisions, the Alternative Annotator Test (Alt-Test) was introduced for dense settings where all items are annotated by the same annotators. However, in many large-scale annotation settings, items are annotated by different subsets of annotators. We therefore propose the Alternative Annotator Test with Resampled Annotations (AltRA-Test), a statistical test that does not require that all items are annotated by the same annotators. AltRA-Test uses a bootstrap that resamples items, draws k human annotations for each item, and substitutes one of them with an LLM annotation. This produces paired all-human and mixed human-LLM panels. A replacement is supported when the inter-annotator agreement (IAA) of the mixed panel is statistically non-inferior to the IAA of the all-human panel, i.e., when the LLM preserves the signal that the human annotators share. We establish that AltRA-Test is a consistent test of asymptotic level alpha. We then evaluate it through simulations and real-world experiments in which we test 18 LLMs and 5 prompting techniques on 20 datasets across text, image, audio, and video. Across these evaluations, about 100 items often suffice for the test. In simulations, where we know whether the LLM is a better or a worse annotator than the humans, AltRA-Test makes more correct replacement decisions than existing baselines. In real-world data experiments, LLMs pass the test in about half of the setups, depending mainly on the task. Since replacement is not always justified, we encourage researchers to test it for their task.
articles.title_zh: Altra-Test:对没有共同注释员的LLM法官的替代注释员测试

articles.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.26809v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are increasingly deployed with access to search tools at inference. Yet pretraining remains predominantly focused on predicting static text, with search capabilities typically introduced during post-training. We propose Search-Native Pretraining as a practical route to teach search capability during pretraining from ordinary text corpora. Specifically, we augment pretraining corpus at scale with web-search queries and retrieve web response using a local index. Training on this augmented corpus teaches models to generate search calls and incorporate retrieved evidence during language modeling. Across Wikipedia and DCLM-Edu corpora and 360M to 3.3B parameter scales, search-pretrained models ("QueryLM") show improved performance on knowledge-intensive tasks and higher steerability toward the retrieved evidence. Crucially, their advantage persists after supervised fine-tuning of both search-pretrained and conventionally pretrained models, indicating that the tested post-training procedures do not fully recover the capabilities developed during pretraining. Throughout our experiments, we find that a 1.4B QueryLM consistently beats or matches the performance of a FLOP-matched 3.3B baseline model across all knowledge intensive tasks. These results establish search-pretraining as a practical way to develop foundational search capabilities during pretraining. We release the training artifacts, including model checkpoints and data.
articles.title_zh: 从开始搜索:语言模型的搜索- Native Pretraining

articles.title: Isolating the Language Shell: A Content-Controlled Study of Multilingual Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.27053v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multilingual reasoning distillation requires choosing the language in which teacher reasoning is presented, yet existing recipes often entangle linguistic form with differences in generation, translation, and filtering. We construct content-controlled supervision by rendering the same verified English trajectories into English, translated target-language, and language-mixed shells, and fine-tune two pretrained students in three target languages, evaluating them on multilingual mathematical reasoning at two difficulty levels. Even with the underlying reasoning content held fixed, we find that shell choice can change downstream accuracy, with effects varying across students, languages, and difficulty levels. Pre-training compatibility does not consistently track these outcomes, and even when our tests find no clear accuracy difference between shells, their output-language behavior can still differ substantially. These results suggest that the supervision shell is a distinct design choice in multilingual reasoning distillation.
articles.title_zh: 孤立语言壳:由内容控制的多种语言理由研究

articles.title: Refine, Don't Reinvent: RASA-Bench for Source-Grounded Hindi Prose Refinement
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.29750v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a producer of Hindi creative prose, drafting is cheap and editing is not: a machine-written episode, story, or essay reads as under-written and flat, laced with translationese, and it sometimes quietly alters what the source says. RASA-Bench targets that editing task across three Hindi prose forms, measuring how well a model refines an under-written AI draft, a task distinct from writing from scratch. Across 2,050 drafts and eight refiners (16,400 rewrites), a four-layer protocol credits a rewrite only after it passes a faithfulness check against its own source, then ranks the survivors by holistic editorial preference through per-form Bradley-Terry fits whose centered coefficients are standardized before equal-weight averaging. Staying faithful proves to be a decisive test that behaves differently by form: gate-failure rates range from 9.1% on short stories to 29.5% on audio fiction, and the drift that disqualifies a rewrite shifts from events and identity in narrative to claims and evidence in essays. A 600-case human audit puts gate agreement at 0.925 (0.91 to 0.94 across forms), whereas subjective preference is form-sensitive and least settled for essays, among human readers no less than the model judge. The benchmark, evaluation protocol, and Hindi prose diagnostics are available at https://abdur75648.github.io/rasa-bench.
articles.title_zh: 精准,不要修补:RASA-Bench 用于源头齐全的印地语

articles.title: Task-Dependent Linguistic Measures in Aphasia Discourse: A Comparative Analysis of Narrative, Descriptive, and Procedural Speech
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.30826v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Background: Transcript-based measures such as word counts, lexical diversity and disfluency rates are widely used to describe language ability in aphasia. Each measure comes from a specific elicitation task, and studies use different tasks, so values from different tasks may not be comparable. Aims: To test whether discourse tasks change these measures within the same speakers, and whether the measures follow a gradient from Procedural to Descriptive to Narrative discourse. Methods & Procedures: Baseline transcripts from 61 adults with chronic post-stroke aphasia were taken from the Fridriksson-2 corpus in AphasiaBank (POLAR trial, registered as NCT03416738). Each speaker produced a Procedural (Sandwich), a Descriptive (Broken Window) and a Narrative (Cinderella) sample in one session. A rule-based pipeline extracted 13 measures, 10 of which were common enough to test. Friedman, Page and Wilcoxon tests with false discovery rate correction were used, with a speaker-grouped Random Forest classifier as a supporting check. Outcomes & Results: Total words and number of different words followed the full gradient, but the step from Procedural to Descriptive was small. For most other measures, Narrative stood apart, while Descriptive and Procedural did not differ. Among the 31 speakers with at least 25 words in every task, filler rate, repetition rate and total disfluency density were higher in Narrative than in both other tasks. The classifier reached an accuracy of 0.61 (always guessing the most common task would give 0.41), mainly by recognizing Narrative samples. Conclusions: Discourse tasks are not interchangeable, and expressing disfluencies per word does not remove the task effect. The task should be reported with every measure, and values should be compared only within the same task.
articles.title_zh: 《阿法西亚演讲中的任务依赖语言措施:叙述、描述和程序发言的比较分析》

articles.title: United in Diversity? Contextual Biases in LLM-Based Predictions of the 2024 European Parliament Elections
articles.summary: arXiv:2409.09045v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: "Silicon samples" based on large language models (LLMs) have been argued to serve as efficient alternatives to surveys of humans, assuming that their training data includes information on human attitudes and behavior. However, LLM-generated survey data might exhibit biases, for example due to a lack of diversity in training and alignment processes, which risk reinforcing existing biases in research and policymaking. In this study, we examine to what extent LLM-based predictions of individual public opinion exhibit context-dependent biases by predicting the results of the 2024 EU elections. Before the elections have taken place, we prompt three LLMs with individual-level background information of 26,000 eligible European voters to predict each person's voting behavior. We show that when compared to the actual results, LLM-based predictions of future voting behavior largely fail, their accuracy is unequally distributed across national and linguistic contexts, and they require detailed attitudinal information in the prompt. The findings emphasize the limited applicability of silicon samples to public opinion prediction. In investigating their contextual biases, this study contributes to the understanding and mitigation of inequalities in the development of LLMs and their applications in computational social science.
articles.title_zh: 多样性联合? 2024年欧洲议会选举基于LLM的预测的背景比喻

articles.title: MathArena: Evaluating LLMs on Uncontaminated Math Competitions
articles.summary: arXiv:2505.23281v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The rapid advancement of reasoning capabilities in large language models (LLMs) has led to notable improvements on mathematical benchmarks. However, many of the most commonly used evaluation datasets (e.g., AIME 2024) are widely available online, making it difficult to disentangle genuine reasoning from potential memorization. Furthermore, these benchmarks do not evaluate proof-writing capabilities, which are crucial for many mathematical tasks. To address this, we introduce MathArena, a new benchmark based on the following key insight: recurring math competitions provide a stream of high-quality, challenging problems that can be used for real-time evaluation of LLMs. By evaluating models as soon as new problems are released, we effectively eliminate the risk of contamination. Using this framework, we find strong signs of contamination in AIME 2024. Nonetheless, evaluations on harder competitions, such as CMIMC 2025, demonstrate impressive reasoning capabilities in top-performing models. MathArena is also the first benchmark for proof-writing capabilities. On IMO 2025, top models achieve slightly less than 40%, demonstrating both notable progress and significant room for improvement. So far, we have evaluated over $50$ models across seven competitions, totaling $162$ problems. As an evolving benchmark, MathArena will continue to track the progress of LLMs on newly released competitions, ensuring rigorous and up-to-date evaluation of mathematical reasoning.
articles.title_zh: MathArena:评估未受污染的数学竞赛法学硕士学位

articles.title: GDS Agent for Graph Algorithmic Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2508.20637v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable multimodal information processing and reasoning ability. When equipped with tools through function calling and enhanced with retrieval-augmented techniques, compound LLM-based systems can access closed data sources and answer questions about them. However, they still struggle to process and reason over large-scale graph-structure data. In this technical report we introduce the GDS (Graph Data Science) agent. The GDS agent introduces a comprehensive set of graph algorithms as tools, together with preprocessing (retrieval) and postprocessing of algorithm results, in a model context protocol (MCP) server. It is accompanied by a skill that guides the LLM through graph analysis. The agent can be used with any modern LLM out-of-the-box. GDS agent allows users to ask any question that implicitly and intrinsically requires graph algorithmic reasoning about their data, and quickly obtain accurate and grounded answers. We introduce new benchmarks that evaluate intermediate tool calls as well as final responses, and the results indicate that the GDS agent solves a wide spectrum of graph tasks. We also demonstrate how the GDS agent can perform open-ended analyses at the level of domain experts, on tasks such as money laundering tracing and pattern mining in biology. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and the future roadmap.
articles.title_zh: GDS 图形算法解释代理

articles.title: AI-Mediated Communication Can Reduce Opinion-Based Network Segregation
articles.summary: arXiv:2510.21984v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Everyday communication is increasingly AI-mediated, with large language models (LLMs) suggesting wording, tone, and framing while humans decide whether to adopt them. Because communication can shape who people choose to interact with, the effects of AI mediation may extend beyond individual attitudes and perceptions to broader patterns of network segregation across opinion differences. Here, we examine this possibility through a preregistered online experiment (N=711 across 80 sessions) in which participants discussed controversial political topics over multiple rounds and could freely reorganize into groups. During the discussions, participants received LLM-generated message suggestions under either individual AI assistance centered on participants' own stances or relational AI assistance incorporating group members' perspectives. We find that individual and relational AI assistance produced distinct trajectories of opinion-based network segregation. Segregation remained largely unchanged under individual AI assistance but decreased significantly under relational AI assistance. Even though many participants adopted few or no AI-generated suggestions, relational AI assistance significantly increased positive sentiment in group discussions. More positive conversations then helped sustain more opinion-diverse groups. The relational communication strategy had no detectable network-level effect when presented as direct instruction to participants, suggesting that AI scaffolding contributed to the observed reduction in segregation. Incorporating the perspectives of social partners into AI-mediated communication can reduce opinion-based network segregation.
articles.title_zh: AI-经修改的通信可以减少基于意见的网络隔离

articles.title: Shadows in the Code: Exploring the Risks and Defenses of LLM-based Multi-Agent Software Development Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2511.18467v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Model (LLM)-driven multi-agent systems has significantly streamlined software developing tasks, enabling users with little technical expertise to develop executable applications. While these systems democratize software creation through natural language requirements, they introduce significant security risks that remain largely unexplored. We identify two risky scenarios: Malicious User with Benign Agents (MU-BA) and Benign User with Malicious Agents (BU-MA). We introduce the Implicit Malicious Behavior Injection Attack (IMBIA), demonstrating how multi-agent systems can be manipulated to generate software with concealed malicious capabilities beneath seemingly benign applications, and propose Adv-IMBIA as a defense mechanism. Evaluations across ChatDev, MetaGPT, and AgentVerse frameworks reveal varying vulnerability patterns, with IMBIA achieving attack success rates of 93%, 45%, and 71% in MU-BA scenarios, and 71%, 84%, and 45% in BU-MA scenarios. Our defense mechanism reduced attack success rates significantly, particularly in the MU-BA scenario. Further analysis reveals that compromised agents in the coding and testing phases pose significantly greater security risks, while also identifying critical agents that require protection against malicious user exploitation. Our findings highlight the urgent need for robust security measures in multi-agent software development systems and provide practical guidelines for implementing targeted, resource-efficient defensive strategies.
articles.title_zh: 代码中的阴影:探索基于LM的多代理软件开发系统的风险和防御

articles.title: Network of Theseus (like the ship)
articles.summary: arXiv:2512.04198v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A standard assumption in deep learning is that the inductive bias introduced by a neural network architecture must persist from training through inference. The architecture you train with is the architecture you deploy. This assumption constrains the community from selecting architectures that may have desirable efficiency or design properties due to difficulties with optimization. We challenge this assumption with the Network of Theseus (NoT), a method for progressively converting a trained, or even untrained, guide network architecture part-by-part into an entirely different target network architecture while preserving the performance of the guide network. At each stage, components in the guide network architecture are incrementally replaced with the target architecture modules and aligned via representational similarity metrics. This procedure preserves most of the functionality of the guide network even under substantial architectural changes-for example, converting a convolutional network into a multilayer perceptron, or GPT-2 into a recurrent neural network. By decoupling optimization from deployment, NoT expands the space of viable inference-time architectures, opening opportunities for better accuracy-efficiency tradeoffs and enabling more directed exploration of the architectural design space.
articles.title_zh: 特修斯网络(如飞船)

articles.title: Neural Isomorphic Fields: A Transformer-based Algebraic Numerical Embedding
articles.summary: arXiv:2601.12095v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural network models often face challenges when processing very small or very large numbers due to issues such as overflow, underflow, and unstable output variations. To mitigate these problems, we propose using embedding vectors for numbers instead of directly using their raw values. These embeddings aim to retain essential algebraic properties while preventing numerical instabilities. We introduce Neural Isomorphic Fields (NIF), a digit-sequence Transformer autoencoder trained with two learned commutative operators and an antisymmetric neural comparator. At zero loss, the embeddings provably form an ordered integral domain isomorphic to the decimal fractions, whose field of fractions is isomorphic to the rationals. For the trained model, we bound errors of operations, chains and algebraic laws by decoding margins, defects and Lipschitz constants. Trained on up to 25 digits, NIF reaches at least 99.9% exact match on closure, identity, associativity and distributivity and 99.8% on ten-step chains and the order relation. With four channels per decimal place, reconstruction and both operations exceed 99.7% exact match on numbers of up to 200 digits whose parts stay within training lengths, so the dimension grows linearly. In a language model, frozen operators raise exact match on 14-20-digit word problems from 12.0% (operators off) to 39.7%.
articles.title_zh: 神经异形场:一个基于变形器的代数嵌入

articles.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Cognitive Complexity in LLMs via Linear Probing using Bloom's Taxonomy
articles.summary: arXiv:2602.17229v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The black-box nature of Large Language Models necessitates novel evaluation frameworks that transcend surface-level performance metrics. This study investigates the internal neural representations of the levels of complexity using Bloom's Taxonomy as a hierarchical lens. By analyzing high-dimensional activation vectors from different LLMs, we probe whether different Bloom levels, ranging from basic recall (Remember) to abstract synthesis (Create), are linearly separable within the model's residual streams. Our results demonstrate that linear classifiers achieve high accuracy across all Bloom levels, providing evidence that level information is encoded in a linearly accessible subspace of the model's representations. These findings provide evidence that the model organizes representations according to Bloom categories early in the forward pass, with representations becoming increasingly separable across layers.
articles.title_zh: 通过使用 Bloom 分类学的线性测试对LLMs 中认知复杂度的机械解释

articles.title: Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Latent Chain-of-Thought with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization
articles.summary: arXiv:2603.21676v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Standard Transformers have a fixed computational depth, limiting their ability to generalize to tasks that require variable-depth reasoning. The usual remedy, Chain-of-Thought (CoT), spends tokens to reason, inflating the key--value cache, so memory becomes the limiting cost when reasoning is served over large query batches. We study a depth-recurrent Transformer that decouples computational depth from parameter count by iterating a shared-weight block, so that adding reasoning steps leaves peak inference memory unchanged and grows latency only linearly, with no token generation. Three ingredients support the recurrence over 20+ thinking steps: a silent thinking objective that supervises only the final output, LayerScale initialization, and an identity-biased gate that opens a gradient highway across steps. We characterize it on three compositional domains with decreasing structural bias: graph reachability (adjacency masking), nested boolean logic (relative positioning), and unstructured relational text (no structural positional cue). We find a \emph{computational frontier}: accuracy climbs once the thinking-step count meets the task's complexity, reaching near-perfect performance on the two structured tasks and a lower plateau on unstructured text. How it climbs depends on the structural bias---abruptly from chance on the graph task, gradually on the other two. Depth recurrence extrapolates beyond the training range: it succeeds on the graph task where fixed-depth models barely extrapolate, and on the two sequence tasks comes within two points of fixed-depth Transformers that use $4$--$6.4\times$ more parameters. On the graph task, whose adjacency mask makes propagation depth verifiable, intermediate per-step supervision---a standard recipe for deep iterative models---consistently \emph{harms} this extrapolation at widths $d \geq 256$. We release the code for reproducibility.
articles.title_zh: 深思深想,不长思深想:内存-有效后端链-与深度-再流变换器一起思考,用于组成概括

articles.title: NSFL: A Post-Training Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzy Logic Framework for Boolean Operators in Neural Embeddings
articles.summary: arXiv:2604.10604v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Standard dense retrievers have no native mechanism for multi-atom logical constraints. We introduce Neuro-Symbolic Fuzzy Logic (NSFL), a training-free framework that brings fuzzy-logical structure to neural embedding spaces through a first-order finite-difference treatment of similarity. NSFL anchors logical operations on zero-order atomic scores while steering with Neuro-Symbolic Deltas (NS-Delta) -- the marginal semantic contributions induced by contextual fusion -- preserving atomic meaning while capturing contextual dependence, and avoiding the representation collapse and manifold escape endemic to geometric baselines. For latency-constrained deployment, Spherical Query Optimization (SQO) uses Riemannian optimization to project logical formulas into manifold-stable query vectors. Across six encoder configurations and two modalities, NSFL yields mAP@100 improvements up to +81% on QUEST and +70% on a COCO-derived text-to-image benchmark, and provides an additive +19% average gain on an encoder already fine-tuned for logical retrieval. On NevIR, where absolute accuracies are directly interpretable, NSFL doubles pairwise accuracy -- NevIR's both-correct criterion -- from 0.256 to 0.508. The decomposition is exact and general; the operators built on it are engineering realizations rather than a closed algebra, and we state that boundary precisely. Code is available at https://github.com/vladiaidev-lab/NSFL
articles.title_zh: NSFL:神经嵌入器中布尔操作器的后训练神经系统模糊逻辑框架

articles.title: Search-E1: Self-Distillation Drives Self-Evolution in Search-Augmented Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2605.22511v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Outcome based reinforcement learning provides a simple and effective recipe for training search augmented reasoning agents. Recent work seeks further improvements through stronger external teachers, auxiliary process supervision, specialized reward shaping, and increasingly elaborate training pipelines. This raises a natural question: can agents continue improving by learning from their own successful experience? We present Search-E1, a simple self evolution framework that alternates vanilla GRPO with on policy self distillation (OPSD). After each GRPO round, Search-E1 mines sibling trajectories generated by the policy itself and exposes the search skeleton of an efficient successful trajectory, that is, the sequence of queries it issued, as privileged context. A token level forward KL objective then aligns the policy under its standard inference context with its own distribution under this privileged context. In this way, the policy converts contrasts among its own rollouts into dense token level supervision without an external teacher, auxiliary reward model, or annotation beyond reference answers. On seven single hop and multi hop QA benchmarks, Search-E1 reaches an average Exact Match of 0.440 with Qwen2.5-3B and 0.482 with Qwen2.5-7B, the highest seven-benchmark averages in our comparison. These results show that alternating outcome based exploration with self distillation provides a simple and effective path to iterative improvement in search augmented reasoning
articles.title_zh: 搜索- E1: 自我分裂驱动 搜索强化原因中的自我演变

articles.title: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2606.11078v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Various test-time interventions for Computer Use Agents (CUAs), including critic models, have been developed to improve performance through pre-execution action evaluation in complex Graphical User Interface (GUI) environments. However, existing critics suffer from two key limitations: they (1) focus primarily on short-sighted decision loops (e.g., forgetting earlier actions) and (2) lack the visual grounding needed to detect flawed actions (e.g., clicking wrong UI elements). To address these, we introduce HiViG, a History-aware Visually Grounded test-time framework, built around a multimodal critic trained on real GUI trajectories to abstract past interactions into a compact record and to evaluate actions with visual grounding. At test time, HiViG integrates the critic into the policy decision loop to provide macro-action history, which summarizes the policy's completed achievements, and visually grounded critique, which verifies raw execution coordinates against the current screenshot to intercept errors before execution. Across web, mobile, and desktop benchmarks, HiViG consistently outperforms existing scalar and verbal critics, improving average success rates over the strongest baseline by 5.8% for Qwen3-VL-32B and 9.0% for Gemini-3-Flash, and demonstrates strong cross-platform generalization. Ablations show that macro-action history mitigates short-sighted planning and visually grounded critique reduces execution errors, with both components being critical for test-time scaling in long-horizon GUI tasks.
articles.title_zh: 对计算机使用智能体的目视批评

articles.title: Safe Inference-Time Alignment via Lagrangian Reward Augmentation
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.02781v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Inference-time alignment steers a frozen language model during decoding using auxiliary reward signals, avoiding the cost of repeated weight updates. However, existing inference-time alignment methods typically optimize a single scalar score, so explicit safety constraints must either be ignored or encoded through manually tuned penalties. We propose Lagrangian Reward Augmentation (LARA), a general inference-time alignment framework under safety constraints. Starting from a KL-regularized constrained objective with a reward model and a cost model, LARA dualizes the constraint and reduces the optimization problem to a one-dimensional convex problem over a nonnegative dual variable. Estimated on a small calibration set, this dual variable defines an augmented reward that can be used as a drop-in scoring signal within existing inference-time alignment methods. For sequence-level sampling methods, such as Best-of-N reranking, the calibrated dual variable corresponds to the solution of the expected-cost constrained problem. For token-level reward-guided decoding methods, the same construction yields a principled dual-calibrated heuristic rather than an exact constrained-policy guarantee. We evaluate LARA on both sequence-level and token-level inference-time alignment methods, and find that LARA improves the helpfulness-harmlessness tradeoff, with Best-of-N achieving the best performance among inference-time methods, approaching finetuning-based direct alignment baselines.
articles.title_zh: 通过Lagrangian奖励增强的安全推断-时间调整

articles.title: Information Discernment in Large Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2607.19355v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used with external knowledge sources like the internet. Do they weigh information appropriately -- updating more for reliable sources (source discernment) and more when claims bring priors closer to the truth (truth discernment)? We formalize this as information discernment and introduce Learn2Discern (L2D), an experimental framework and benchmark grounded in three normative axioms with interpretable metrics. To establish external validity, a pre-registered, quota-matched user study (n=299) confirms that real LLM users endorse all three axioms and report that violations reduce their trust and usage intent. Across 13 models and nearly 670K trials, we find consistent failures across both dimensions: models perform near chance on source and truth discernment, rely on source popularity twice as much as source reliability, and update roughly equally whether a claim improves or worsens their position relative to the ground truth. Models integrate external knowledge most effectively on datasets where their priors are already the most accurate. Newer and larger models improve truth discernment but not source discernment, a blind spot that model complexity does not address. We identify simple inference-time interventions that improve both forms of discernment. We release our dataset and survey as a testbed for a core alignment property that scales in importance as LLMs replace traditional search.
articles.title_zh: 大语言模型中的信息解析

articles.title: AVA-Encoder: Learning to Represent Videos via Reconstruction-Driven Agentic Self-Evolution
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.12313v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Agentic video creation systems remain far from cinematic-grade quality: their underlying models struggle to plan how story, characters, visuals, and sound fit together, and high-quality creation trajectories to learn such planning abilities are scarce. Finished human films embody this knowledge, but in a tightly coupled audiovisual form that agents cannot directly read or manipulate. We propose the Agentic Video "Auto-Encoder" (AVA-Encoder), which works backward from human films, turning them into agent-native video representations with reconstruction itself as the sole supervision. It encodes a film into a Film Knowledge Graph (Film KG) of structured-text nodes, typed dependency edges, and linked multimodal assets, then regenerates the film from this graph with a fixed decoder. Crucially, by distilling reconstruction residuals into textual gradients, AVA-Encoder drives a dual-loop self-evolution: an outer loop autonomously discovers a generalizable encoding strategy entirely from unlabeled videos, while an inner loop refines each video's Film KG at test time. AVA-Encoder improves reconstruction fidelity by 20.9 percentage points over the strongest baseline, and its autonomously learned strategy outperforms a human-tuned strategy using 70% fewer prompt tokens. Our representations drive three downstream breakthroughs: (1) Film KGs enable coordinated graph-based editing and (2) improve one-shot video generation across four open-source frameworks, while (3) fine-tuning agents on our reverse-engineered trajectories boosts video creation quality by 38.7%. We release the framework and a dataset of 500 Film KGs with over 27,000 creation trajectories.
articles.title_zh: AVA- Encoder: 学习通过重建- Driven代理自我进化来代表视频

articles.title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.21240v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Presenting the same request with different context or formatting can change which sparse autoencoder (SAE) features respond inside a language model. Understanding these changes raises two questions. Which feature responses recur across related inputs, and which of them contribute to downstream computation? We study this phenomenon as representation redistribution and introduce the redistribution sensitivity score (RSS) to identify large feature changes that recur in a consistent direction. We select features on one set of prompt variants and evaluate them on separate variants. Across 27 pretrained SAEs spanning eight language models, RSS reveals a consistent pattern of redistribution. Context and wrapper transformations produce stronger recurring responses than local edits. We then use two frozen safety readouts to measure how these changes contribute to downstream computation. RSS identifies features with approximately twice the mean held out contribution of features selected by the largest readout coefficients, using activation responses alone. An exact decomposition explains how feature changes and readout coefficients determine their effects on the decision margin. Combining RSS contributions with the clean margin improves recurrent failure AUROC from 0.863 to 0.935 and from 0.901 to 0.958, approaching the full readout results of 0.965 and 0.964. These findings show that recurring changes in sparse representations provide a way to identify features with meaningful downstream contributions. Code is available at https://github.com/OpenSAE/Redistribution-Sensitivity-Score.
articles.title_zh: Sparse 自动编码器中的重排

articles.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.18359v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.
articles.title_zh: 设想代理机器人:机器人系统的新时代

articles.title: NONSENSE: Non-Semantic Strings Expose Semanticity Gaps in Dense Retrieval
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.22353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dense retrieval is central to modern search, question answering, and retrieval-augmented generation, where high similarity is often treated as evidence of semantic relevance. We stress-test this assumption with NONSENSE, a black-box optimization framework that constructs visibly non-semantic strings by optimizing only their dense similarity to the query. Across seven retrieval datasets and five single-vector retrievers, these strings frequently outscore the retriever's own best judged query-relevant passage (QRP) and often rank first in the full corpus. The result indicates a semanticity gap in the evaluated dense retrievers: strings with no coherent passage-level semantic content can lie closer to the query in embedding space than genuine relevant evidence. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating dense retrievers not only by whether they retrieve relevant documents, but also by whether their similarity scores reliably reflect semantic evidence.
articles.title_zh: 无语:非语义字符串 Expose 语义差距 ense Retrieval

articles.title: Bias Cascade: Understanding the Gap Between Knowledge Alignment and Effect Replication in LLM-based Social Simulation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.28854v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate participants in social experiments. Existing research has primarily focused on aligning social knowledge and isolated responses, while overlooking whether simulations can reproduce the collective effects of social interventions. This distinction is critical due to a failure mechanism we call a $bias$ $cascade$: similar individual states can lead to different actions, while agreement on isolated actions can still produce divergent outcomes through dynamic interactions. As a result, models may produce accurate social judgments yet fail to reproduce the outcomes of classic human studies. To investigate this problem empirically, we introduce $REFLEX$ (Reproducing Effects of Foundational Literature EXperiments), a benchmark of 30 counterfactual social experiments grounded in classic human studies that compares knowledge judgment with effect simulation. Knowledge judgment directly predicts the direction of an intervention's effect, whereas effect simulation fixes the scenario and participants while varying one prespecified social factor, with agents generating actions from local observations that are aggregated into macro-level average treatment effects. Compared with human-study findings, the best-performing model achieves net directional scores of 0.847 for knowledge judgment and 0.453 for effect simulation. Moreover, longer causal chains are associated with poorer effect replication, consistent with the bias-cascade hypothesis. These findings reveal a substantial gap between knowledge alignment and effect replication, showing that current LLMs remain inadequate for reliably simulating collective human behavior.
articles.title_zh: Bias Cascade:理解基于LLM的社会模拟中知识协调与效果复制之间的差距

articles.title: Learning the Platform, Not the Learner: Sequencing Shortcuts in the Offline Evaluation of Educational Recommender Systems and LLM Rankers
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33240v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Educational recommenders are usually compared offline, by how well they predict the next activity in logs of tutoring systems, learning applications and MOOCs, where the next activity is largely decided by the platform: teachers assign problem sets, tutors draw problems until mastery, engines select questions. On eight public datasets from five platforms, we compare four structural predictors, which use nothing about the learner beyond the last activity, with ten personalised recommenders and with open-weight LLM rankers from 0.5 to 7 billion parameters, under two protocols. The structural predictors reach between 0.81 and 1.00 of the best accuracy of any method (median 0.95), mostly through population transitions rather than the course order; the best personalised recommender is significantly better on five datasets, by 0.007 to 0.102 NDCG@10, and on Eedi in three of four training runs. Every method is far less accurate on steps along transitions never seen in training and on steps chosen by learners. LLM rankers look competent with random negatives but are never much better than a word-matching baseline, and with negatives that are plausible under the course structure they stay close to random or well behind the transition heuristic, whatever their size. In a simulation with known learner needs, the structural share tracks the share of steps decided by the platform, and offline accuracy ranks an oracle of the learners' needs below imitators of the platform. Weighting test steps by how unlikely the structure makes them restores much of the link with usefulness and, on the real data, reveals a significant personalisation signal on seven of the eight datasets. We propose a syllabus-aware evaluation checklist and release a Python package that reports the lift of any recommender over the structure.
articles.title_zh: 学习平台,而不是学习者:在教育推荐系统和LLM Rankers的离线评价中排列快捷键

articles.title: Multi-Modal Causal Disentanglement for Multi-Domain Sequential Audio Recommendation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern music platforms expose users to heterogeneous audio content domains such as songs, playlists, and podcasts. Multi-domain sequential recommendation (MDSR) seeks to exploit such cross-domain behavior, yet two obstacles persist in practice. First, joint optimization across heterogeneous domains is prone to negative transfer, with high-traffic domains dominating the shared parameter space and suppressing weaker domains. Second, conventional ID-based collaborative signals fail to bridge domains that are semantically related but exhibit little behavioral overlap. This paper presents CAMAR, a multi-modal causal disentanglement framework for multi-domain audio recommendation. From a causal perspective, user behavior is modeled as the joint outcome of a domain-invariant preference and domain-specific preferences. Guided by this view, CAMAR factorizes user representations into domain-invariant and domain-specific components and enforces domain adversarial invariance together with orthogonality, restricting cross-domain interaction to the invariant subspace and suppressing harmful transfer paths. To strengthen cross-domain semantic coupling, CAMAR derives trainable semantic-ID embeddings from pre-trained text, vision, and audio features through residual quantization, yielding an end-to-end multi-modal adaptation tailored to recommendation. A transfer network imputes user representations for inactive domains, mitigating cross-domain cold start. Experiments on both public and industrial datasets demonstrate consistent gains over strong baselines. In online A/B tests on NetEase Cloud Music, one of China's largest music streaming platforms, CAMAR delivers consistent gains across all three domains in their main traffic scenarios, validating its effectiveness in multi-domain audio recommendation at scale.
articles.title_zh: 多域序列音频建议中的多模块分解

articles.title: Structure-Aware Multimodal Retrieval Under Data Scarcity, Privacy Constraints and Out-of-Domain Content
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose: Figure retrieval from reference atlases in expert domains like forensic pathology, dentistry and geology must work without labels or training pairs, on content that often cannot leave local hardware, and on images outside the training data of image-text encoders. This work proposes a structure-aware pipeline that satisfies all three, retrieving figures through the page structure recovered by layout geometry and a local open-weight 8B VLM. Methods: A geometry-based pairing method is introduced, in which the model receives a schematic of the detected boxes and selects each picture's caption without access to pixels or text. Caption retrieval is evaluated on three private corpora (29 books, 10,421 figures, 218 queries) with blind human grading, against a lexical baseline, generated descriptions and five image-text encoders. Results: Geometric pairing was correct for 96%, 92% and 77% of pictures in the three domains, against 76%, 45% and 53% for the better of two document parsers. A hosted model given the schematic was equally accurate, while coordinates as text lost 22 points. Caption retrieval obtained an nDCG@5 of 0.85, 0.87 and 0.76, against 0.54, 0.51 and 0.27 for the best cross-modal encoder and 0.41, 0.28 and 0.30 for generated descriptions. Pairing errors carried over to retrieval. Conclusion: The proposed pipeline achieves accurate figure retrieval with small local models and no in-domain training, where general and biomedical image-text encoders fall far behind. Its geometry-only pairing is the most accurate of five methods and exposes no content, even to a hosted model. Code and prompts are released.
articles.title_zh: 数据稀缺、隐私限制和域外内容下的智能多式联运检索

articles.title: Privacy-Aware Adaptive Client Selection for Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated retrieval-augmented generation retrieves evidence from distributed corpora. However, broadcasting queries to all clients increases the retrieval burden and query exposure. We present Privacy-Aware Adaptive Client Selection for Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation (PACS-FedRAG), an online selector that takes into account perturbed semantic profiles along with evidence feedback, latency, payload cost, and exploration. In a ten-client setting where three clients are chosen, the archived end-to-end benchmark reports an evidence overlap of 0.372 and an answer accuracy of 0.287. The retrieval-only evaluation, on the other hand, reuses a full-broadcast baseline with a different fusion tie-breaking policy. Rank fusion across disjoint client corpora imposes an overlap ceiling of 0.375, limiting its interpretation as a relevance measure. Answer accuracy is below the fixed-label diagnostic of 0.645, and raw generator responses are unavailable for parser verification. Corrected baselines and a new answer-level evaluation are needed to assess whether quality is preserved. Selecting three clients reduces the number of query recipients by 70%. Profile perturbation does not provide confidentiality of queries or passages.
articles.title_zh: 为联邦报复强化世代选择自觉适应客户端

articles.title: MulCLIP: A Multi-level Alignment Framework for Enhancing Fine-grained Long-context CLIP
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models such as CLIP excel at image-text alignment but struggle with long, detailed descriptions due to training on short captions. Recent methods address this limitation using region proposals to align visual regions with sentences, but at substantial deployment cost. We present MulCLIP, an end-to-end multi-level alignment framework that directly exploits natural long-text structure without region proposals. Instead of simply stacking objectives, MulCLIP aligns different textual granularities through compatible training signals: global contrastive alignment for long captions and short summaries, Word-Patch Reconstruction over locally calibrated features for within-sample word-patch semantics, and Subcaption-Aggregated Patch alignment for context-rich subcaption grounding. Experiments on benchmarks spanning varying caption lengths show consistent gains, and ablations confirm that the proposed objectives are complementary and jointly improve the overall framework. Code will be released at https://github.com/truongchau2602/MulCLIP.
articles.title_zh: MulCLIP:加强精细长文本的多层次协调框架 CLIP

articles.title: RecField: Embedding Recommendations into Spatial Movie Organization as Affordances for Serendipitous Encounters
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Research on serendipity-oriented recommender systems has focused on algorithms that recommend unexpected yet useful items. However, serendipity is increasingly viewed as a user experience shaped by both algorithmic outputs and system features. This study positions recommendations not as the primary goal users pursue but as an environmental affordance that creates opportunities for discovery during other activities. We propose RecField, a spatial movie organization interface where users freely arrange movies into collection zones. For each collection, RecField provides attribute-based recommendation lists labeled according to their recommendation perspectives. A between-subjects experiment ($N$ = 57) examined the effects of recommendations on discoveries made during a foreground task of creating and organizing personal movie profiles. Although recommendations did not significantly affect environment-level perceived serendipity, ratings of encounter-related aspects tended to be higher, with small effect sizes. At the individual-movie level, favorites in the recommendation condition received significantly higher ratings for stimulating the desire to watch and broadening preferences, but not for novelty or unexpectedness. Notably, only 14\% of evaluated favorites in the recommendation condition were added directly from recommendation lists. Differences in ratings showed similar effect sizes even when the analysis was restricted to favorites added through other routes. These findings suggest that embedded recommendations can contribute to serendipitous experiences both directly through item acceptance and indirectly by prompting users' own exploration and re-evaluation. They also highlight the value of evaluating serendipity at both the environment and item levels and the limitations of relying solely on direct recommendation acceptance rates.
articles.title_zh: Recfield:将建议将建议纳入空间电影组织,作为满足意外事故需要的费用

articles.title: ConTra: A Training Framework for Effective Contextual Retrieval via Prefix Generation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34366v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data management systems organize large text collections for tasks such as finding relevant studies and extracting contract clauses. Systems make long documents searchable by splitting them into independently indexed chunks. Chunking can separate text from its identifying details. The indexing challenge is to keep each chunk independently searchable while preserving the context needed to find and rank it. Existing methods either encode that context in chunk vectors or attach it as a text prefix. Context encoded only in vectors is unavailable to text rerankers. Prompted prefixes serve both vector search and reranking, but are costly to generate at indexing time and can underperform contextual encoders. We propose ConTra (Context That Travels), a reinforcement learning framework for training lightweight prefix generators. Its reward combines feedback from frozen embedding and reranking models with factual verification and length control. ConTra generates one prefix per chunk during index construction and stores the augmented text and its embedding for reuse across queries. To evaluate contextual retrieval across workloads and under interference, we introduce RealContextBench, a benchmark with five application collections and three controlled conditions that isolate the effect of distracting text. On ConTEB and RealContextBench, ConTra-2B outperforms the prompted 9B baseline using Anthropic's method and the PPLX-4B contextual encoder, with a margin of up to 3.15 points over their best overall scores, while indexing short documents 7.74 times and 2.15 times as fast as those baselines, respectively. Post-trained only on ConTEB, it leads the standalone methods on RealContextBench after reranking and is less sensitive than the prompted 2B baseline to random and topically similar distractors. Code, datasets, and trained models are available at https://github.com/SStan1/ConTra.
articles.title_zh: Contra:通过前缀生成有效背景检索的训练框架

articles.title: Grounding User Preferences in Shared Multimodal Concepts for Recommendation
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal recommendation has substantially advanced item understanding by incorporating rich visual and textual content. Yet user preferences are still commonly encoded as implicit signals tied to individual items, leaving recurring semantic factors without persistent identities that can be shared across items. We introduce MKGE, a multimodal knowledge graph framework that represents these factors as canonical, addressable concepts. MKGE induces a domain-adaptive concept vocabulary from item images and titles, grounds each user's interaction history in supported concepts, and jointly models direct user-item evidence and concept-mediated preference signals. By turning recurring semantics into shared coordinates, MKGE enables evidence from different items to accumulate around the same preference factors. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks demonstrate that MKGE consistently outperforms collaborative, knowledge-graph, multimodal, and recent LLM/MLLM-based recommenders across all six reported metrics. Controlled studies further demonstrate the importance of canonical concept identities and personalized user-concept correspondence, with especially pronounced gains over removing or rewiring the user graph for low-activity users. These results establish canonical multimodal concepts as effective units for preference modeling and transfer. Code, constructed knowledge graphs, and prompts are available at https://github.com/Garden1a-X/MKGE.
articles.title_zh: 共享多式联运概念中的用户优先性

articles.title: Community Notes Across Platforms: Evaluating the Feasibility of Re-using Crowd-sourced Context Notes
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Crowdsourced fact-checking systems such as Community Notes can provide useful context for misleading content. Producing and rating new notes on such systems requires substantial contributor effort. However, the resulting context is typically confined to the post and platform for which it was created. We ask whether already-vetted notes can be reused when the same claims recur across posts and platforms. To investigate this question, we construct a human-labelled dataset using Community Notes attached to X posts created during a one-week period and candidate posts retrieved from Bluesky. Within our observation window, 140 of 340 claims had at least one confirmed recurrence on Bluesky, showing that cross-platform note reuse is a substantial opportunity. Recurrence alone, however, does not establish whether reuse would provide timely context. A timing analysis shows that many relevant notes were already Helpful when matching Bluesky posts appeared. Even when a Bluesky post appeared first, reuse could often still provide context sooner after publication than the original X post received its Helpful note. To automate the discovery of these opportunities, we evaluate a three-stage pipeline that searches the Bluesky stream for potential recurrences and determines whether an existing note applies. The pipeline achieves 72.6% precision in a held-out stream evaluation and 70.1% end-to-end recall on our known-positive set. We further characterize the pipeline's costs and principal failure modes. Crossnote, our prototype Bluesky labeler, implements this approach by applying existing Community Notes to matching posts. Our findings suggest that reusing vetted crowdsourced context is a compelling way to scale the reach and impact of Community Notes. Note reuse can complement the production of new notes by reducing duplicated effort and shortening time to context when misleading claims recur.
articles.title_zh: 跨平台的社区说明:评估重新使用人群源背景说明的可行性

articles.title: KGBridge: Knowledge-Guided Prompt Learning for Non-overlapping Cross-Domain Recommendation
articles.summary: arXiv:2511.02181v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) provide structured relational information, offering a unified semantic foundation for cross-domain recommendation (CDR). Integrating symbolic knowledge with interactions enriches representations, supports reasoning, and enhances interpretability. However, existing methods face three major challenges: (C1) sensitivity to KG sparsity and popularity bias, (C2) reliance on overlapping users for domain alignment, and (C3) insufficient disentanglement between transferable and domain-specific knowledge, which limits stable knowledge transfer. To address these challenges, this paper proposes KGBridge, a knowledge-guided prompt learning framework for non-overlapping cross-domain sequential recommendation. KGBridge comprises: (i) a KG-enhanced prompt encoder that models relation-level semantics as soft prompts, providing structured priors for sequential preference modeling (for C1), and (ii) a two-stage training paradigm combining cross-domain pretraining with privacy-preserving fine-tuning to enable knowledge transfer without shared users (for C2). Furthermore, via correspondence-driven disentanglement, KGBridge explicitly separates domain-shared and domain-specific semantics, preserving their complementarity and stabilizing target-domain adaptation (for C3). Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that KGBridge consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and exhibits robustness under varying KG sparsity, confirming its effectiveness in alleviating structural imbalance and semantic entanglement. To facilitate reproducibility, the source code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/WangYuhan-0520/KGBridge.
articles.title_zh: 克格勃里奇:以知识为指南的不重叠跨领域快速学习建议

articles.title: VulCPE: Context-Aware Cybersecurity Vulnerability Retrieval and Management
articles.summary: arXiv:2505.13895v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The dynamic landscape of cybersecurity demands precise and scalable solutions for vulnerability management in heterogeneous systems, where configuration-specific vulnerabilities are often misidentified due to inconsistent data in databases like the National Vulnerability Database (NVD). Inaccurate Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) data in NVD further leads to false positives and incomplete vulnerability retrieval. Informed by our systematic analysis of CPE and CVEdeails data, revealing more than 50% vendor name inconsistencies, we propose VulCPE, a framework that standardizes data and models configuration dependencies using a unified CPE schema (uCPE), entity recognition, relation extraction, and graph-based modeling. VulCPE achieves superior retrieval precision (0.766) and coverage (0.926) over existing tools. VulCPE ensures precise, context-aware vulnerability management, enhancing cyber resilience.
articles.title_zh: VulCPE:了解背景的网络安全脆弱性检索和管理

articles.title: Code availability is not enough: schemas for documenting and extending data analysis
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A data analysis involves a sequence of decisions, from data cleaning to model specification, each of which can affect the reported result. Reproducing that result is not the same as understanding the sequence of decisions that produced it and the reasons for each: the code mixes those decisions with implementation details, while the manuscript states the major decisions and their rationale but scatters them across its sections and often leaves out the minor ones. A reader may then ask how the result would change under a different decision: the question itself is easy to pose, but implementing it is often non-trivial in practice. In this work, we propose a schema that represents a data analysis as a collection of decisions in natural language, from which large language models (LLMs) can generate and validate analysis scripts directly. This workflow can also expand a single analysis into a full multiverse of alternatives, specified in an alternative file, ready for comparison. We demonstrate the proposed workflow in two applications. In the first, we construct a schema for a published regression analysis of heaped smoking data and show that it reproduces the reported estimates, and that a reviewer-suggested alternative can be specified through the alternative file and turned into code automatically. In the second, where no schema is provided, we show how the workflow serves instead as a reproducibility check, applied to the many-analysts football study. As an intermediate representation between the manuscript and code scripts, our schema gives a self-contained account of an analysis and makes it extensible from a reader's perspective.
articles.title_zh: 代码可用性还不够:记录和扩大数据分析的计划

articles.title: Temporal Exposure to Byzantine Vulnerability Under Intermittent Participation in Federated Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the effect of participation variability on per-round Byzantine vulnerability. We formalise Dynamic Participation Exposure (DPE), a phenomenon in which the global Byzantine fraction remains below an aggregation rule's tolerance threshold, while a participating client set violates, or approaches violation of, the assumptions required for robust aggregation. Under stochastic participation, we derive the probability of per round exposure and analyse how active-set size affects the variability of the observed Byzantine fraction. We further examine the accumulation of exposure over multiple rounds and consider adversaries that selectively participate during favourable rounds. Our analysis shows that intermittent participation does not automatically imply aggregation failure. Rather, it transforms Byzantine robustness from a static population-level property into a stochastic and temporal property. To mitigate this risk, we outline actionable design recommendations based on minimum active-set constraints, temporal monitoring, participation history, and adaptive aggregation.
articles.title_zh: 在不时参与联邦学习的情况下暂时暴露于拜占庭的脆弱性

articles.title: Geophysics-informed invertible operator network for Bayesian geophysical inversion
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geophysical inverse problems are inherently ill-posed because of sparse observations and measurement noise. Classical sampling-based Bayesian inference methods, such as Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), are computationally prohibitive because they require many forward simulations. Data-driven machine-learning methods often struggle to produce physically consistent solutions when training data are limited. To address these issues, we propose a geophysics-informed invertible operator network (GI-ION) that integrates an invertible neural network (INN) within a deep operator-learning framework for efficient Bayesian geophysical inversion. The INN serves as the branch network and transforms the model parameters into branch coefficients that represent the forward solution and a latent variable that captures uncertainty in the inverse problem. By learning the forward operator and enforcing statistical independence between the branch coefficients and the latent variable, GI-ION enables efficient sampling from a learned conditional approximation, even with sparse boundary observations. We validated GI-ION on three representative cases: 1D surface-wave dispersion and travel-time tomography for a 2D synthetic random-field model and a seismic-slice model. Numerical experiments demonstrate robust performance across diverse problem settings and efficient conditional sampling.
articles.title_zh: 贝叶斯地球物理反演的地球物理信息不可逆操作网络

articles.title: Deep Learning-Based Mesoscopic Emission Modeling
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traffic-related emissions are a major contributor to urban air pollution. However, existing emission models face a fundamental trade-off: macroscopic models are computationally efficient but rely on average speeds, leading to systematic errors, while microscopic models achieve high accuracy but are computationally prohibitive for large scale simulations. To bridge this gap, this study introduces Direct Emission Prediction (DEP), a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)-based deep learning model. DEP was trained on over one million synthetic trips generated by coupling real-world GNSS speed profiles with the microscopic emission model MOBSim. By processing sequential link-level inputs, including vehicle characteristics, road attributes, and ambient temperature, DEP predicts CO$_2$ and NOx emissions. We integrated DEP into a MATSim-based workflow and applied it to the Ile-de-France region. DEP matches the accuracy of SPG-M, a hybrid mesoscopic-microscopic reference model, within 0.35% for CO$_2$ and 1.87% for NOx across both hot and cold-start scenarios, while reducing computational runtime to just 2.2%. Furthermore, validation against empirical remote sensing data confirms that DEP accurately reproduces real-world NOx emission levels across Euro 2-6 diesel vehicles, whereas traditional macroscopic tools like COPERT and HBEFA systematically underestimate them. Finally, DEP effectively captures the spatial distribution of cold-start emissions, identifying key hotspots in dense urban areas. This work demonstrates that deep learning-based mesoscopic frameworks can achieve microscopic accuracy at a fraction of the computational cost, enabling scalable, high-resolution urban emission modeling without relying on pre-computed emission factor databases.
articles.title_zh: 深层基于学习的中度排放模型

articles.title: Change Partners at Every Layer: Balanced Random Regrouping for Model Merging
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model merging combines fine-tuned experts into one model that serves many tasks without retraining, but merging many experts this way substantially reduces accuracy. Grouping offers a middle ground: at every layer or weight matrix, the $N$ experts are divided into $K<N$ groups, the experts in a group are merged into one shared module, and a task uses the module merged from its expert's group. Natural choices are to keep the same partners across layers or to group similar experts. Surprisingly, we find that randomly changing partners at every layer outperforms both. We call this Balanced Random Regrouping (BRR): it independently partitions the experts into $K$ equal-sized random groups at each layer (BRR-layer) or weight matrix (BRR-matrix) and merges each group with an existing method. With validation-selected merge scales, both BRR variants outperform reusing one grouping across layers in all 24 CLIP settings, by 1.0-6.8 points, and BRR-matrix also outperforms the similarity-based FlexMerge in every setting. A first-order analysis explains this gain. At each layer, merging a task's expert with its partners shifts the task's output features; when the partners are the same at every layer, these shifts tend to point in similar directions and add up, whereas with new partners at every layer they vary independently and add up less on average. A series of experiments supports this analysis, which further guides a grouping search that can outperform BRR.
articles.title_zh: 改变各层伙伴:平衡随机组合以进行模型合并

articles.title: Sparse Adaptation for In-Context Learning on Data Streams
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) generates massive data streams, making edge computing essential for low-latency applications and 5G networks. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) enable adaptation through in-context examples rather than parameter updates, but evolving streams challenge context relevance and computational efficiency. This work introduces SAIL, a framework for sparse adaptation of TFMs that reuses the model's key--value cache between adaptation events. SAIL reconstructs its support set only when drifts in stream structure indicate potential context inadequacy, while the structural representation itself is updated by changes in predictive performance. SAIL combines prequential error monitoring with online, class-specific micro-clustering to detect changes in cluster mass, class separability, and feature-space coverage. Upon adaptation, a context budget is allocated proportionally to class mass, and the most recently updated micro-clusters provide representative observations for refitting. This limits context redundancy and computational cost while preserving recent structural information.
articles.title_zh: 关于数据流的文本学习的 Sparse 适应

articles.title: FlowersBench: A FluidFlower-Inspired Dataset for Benchmarking Carbon Storage Surrogates Across Geological Structures
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning surrogates are emerging as a computationally efficient tool for uncertainty quantification in geological carbon storage (GCS). Geological structure constitutes a major source of uncertainty; however, existing benchmark simulation datasets predominantly vary petrophysical and operational parameters within a fixed geological setting. Generalisation to unseen geological structures therefore remains largely unexplored. We introduce FlowersBench, a benchmark dataset of 5,000 two-dimensional, reservoir-scale CO$_2$ storage simulations across 244 structural geometries. The geometries are sampled from an in-house structural generator inspired by the FluidFlower experiments and Case B of the 11th Society of Petroleum Engineers Comparative Solution Project (SPE11B). Each simulation is run with Open Porous Media (OPM) Flow over a 50-year injection period and a 500-year post-injection monitoring period. Test geometries are withheld from training to assess generalisation to unseen structural geometries. Two additional subsets support evaluation under structural shift. The first extends the parameter ranges of the structural generator beyond those used for training, and the second introduces an unseen topology of multiple parallel faults. A baseline U-Net surrogate is trained to predict CO$_2$ gas saturation. In representative test cases, the surrogate recovers the main migration pathways, including lateral spreading beneath low-permeability layers and upward flow along fault damage zones, with errors concentrated near the plume boundary.
