We propose Worst-Case Recourse and Graph-Weighted Recourse to find a low-cost action that succeeds across all candidate graphs or a specified fraction of graph weight, respectively. Assuming a set of plausible graphs, for each graph we fit Gaussian process structural equations and assess success using the posterior mean--standard-deviation criterion. We use gradient-based search to determine minimal cost actions and check the validity of the actions on fresh posterior samples. In synthetic and semi-synthetic benchmarks, relaxing robustness, the requirement that an action succeed under every candidate graph, can increase the number of valid recommendations for recourse and lower costs of actions for both methods. In the 20-node GP benchmark, relaxation increases the number of factual instances offered recourse (coverage) from 341 to 436 out of 1,000, while the number of true successes, actions that flip the decision under the generating model, falls from 251 to 184, illustrating the coverage--validity trade-off. Accounting for graph ambiguity can help decision-makers recommend actions that remain effective even when the causal mechanisms of the system are not fully known.
articles.title_zh: 因果关系图下的有力路径

articles.title: BRIAR: Martingale Belief Smoothing on Bifurcation-Guided Reasoning Trees
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has rapidly advanced long-chain reasoning, yet standard policy optimizers distribute rollout compute and gradient credit blindly across a trajectory. On hard problems, an early misstep derails the remaining trace, whereas on solvable problems, the policy keeps generating redundant verification long after the answer is already determined. We trace both pathologies to a single structural fact: under an on-policy verifier, the true prefix pass probability $V^\pi(u)$ along a reasoning trace forms a $[0,1]$-bounded Doob martingale whose learnable credit variance is strictly conserved and bounded above by $V^\pi(u)(1-V^\pi(u))$, vanishing at both the derailed ($V^\pi\to 0$) and absorbed ($V^\pi\to 1$) boundaries. We introduce BRIAR (Bifurcation-guided Rollout and Inference on Adaptive Reasoning trees), a tree-structured RLVR framework built directly around this martingale geometry. First, BRIAR expands discourse-aligned reasoning trees along an upper-confidence outcome-bifurcation frontier, steering rollouts away from absorbed rumination and toward unresolved decision points. Second, it models latent node values with boundary-scaled heteroscedastic edge variances and computes exact global posteriors in linear $\mathcal{O}(|V|)$ time via two-pass Rauch--Tung--Striebel (RTS) tree belief smoothing, eliminating $\mathcal{O}(m^3)$ matrix inversions while gating out spurious boundary noise. Third, BRIAR detects minimal absorbed frontier nodes and applies zero-sum log-length centered suffix advantages strictly post-absorption, leaving pre-absorption derivations provably invariant.
articles.title_zh: BRIAR:对双层树的静电信仰平滑-指导性理性树

articles.title: When to Trust a PFN: Detecting Harmful Shift in Tabular Foundation Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tabular prior-fitted networks (PFNs) work well across tabular classification problems but can fail silently at deployment when distributions shift. We propose CALD (Calibrated Anchor-Loss Disagreement), a lightweight unsupervised monitor that triggers an alarm to warn when a PFN might fail. By finetuning the decoder to maximize disagreement with the test-set prediction while maintaining accuracy on an ID anchor set, CALD identifies harmful OOD batches through the resulting anchor loss, requiring no labels on test batches. We prove that the post-finetune anchor loss has a strictly lower expectation under sufficiently severe shift than under ID eval, yielding a one-sided test. Across 14 datasets covering tabular and structured distribution shift, on both TabPFN and TabICL, CALD matches or outperforms baselines on harmful shifts and is markedly more resilient to benign-shift false alarms.
articles.title_zh: 何时信任一个PFN:检测表格式基础模型中的有害变化

articles.title: Split-RL: Local Conflict Resolution in Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) policies are often trained by mixing contradictory feedback that is localized in space and time. For example, a robot may prioritize speed in open areas versus precision in tight gaps. We introduce Split-RL, a Gradient Boosting Trees (GBT) algorithm that uses guidance labels to locally isolate these conflicting signals. Standard neural networks (NNs) lack the structural mechanism to do this, as their parameters share feedback from all sources. While GBT provides the inductive bias to explicitly partition the state-space per objective, standard tree-fitting procedures aggregate contradictory gradient signals before they reach the leaves. Split-RL leverages this bias to integrate guidance labels into tree construction, routing these updates into disjoint state-space regions and preventing signal interference. Such labels can arise from heuristics, sensor-derived events, or existing rule-based systems, allowing Split-RL to incorporate rule-derived structure while retaining a learned policy. We theoretically show how early gradient aggregation loses objective-specific information and characterize when the Split-RL score isolates conflicting updates. We focus on constrained RL and offline RL with mixed datasets, each balancing two objectives that conflict locally. Across domains with spatial, rare-event, and temporal conflicts, Split-RL consistently outperforms existing methods by meeting the episodic cost budget while maintaining competitive rewards. In offline settings, Split-RL localizes the tradeoff between imitation and policy improvement, outperforming other methods and achieving near-expert performance across varying dataset sizes.
articles.title_zh: Split-RL:加强学习的地方冲突解决

articles.title: Barron Smoothness for Layers in Deep Neural Networks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In order to bound approximation errors for deep neural networks, we split the problem into two steps: First the selection of optimal infinite width limits for each layer and second an optimal discretization of all layers to obtain finite sized networks. We show that in expectation, the latter problem is equivalently characterized by a layer wise generalization of Barron norms. Moreover, we provide an analysis of the optimization landscape and show that local minima are characterized by an equidistribution principle akin to similar ideas in adaptive spline and finite element approximation.
articles.title_zh: 深层神经网络中的巴龙光滑

articles.title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Initialization determines the optimization "fate" of a model, going far beyond just setting the scale of its weights. It establishes a fundamental initial geometry over the input data, dictating certain aspects such as which examples are considered close and which representations gradient descent will naturally refine first. In this paper, we view the initial geometry of a network as an optimization prior and ask whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a completely different architecture. To investigate this question, we use an initialization procedure where a target network is aligned to the representational geometry of a randomly initialized guide network before any downstream training occurs. Crucially, alignment to the guide network cannot transfer learned features, never receives gradients, and does not use labels. We demonstrate that this cross-architecture transfer of "fate" benefits the target network in two key domains: (1) instilling the optimization benefits of depth into shallow networks by aligning them to deeper networks, and (2) transferring representational granularity by using fine-resolution networks to shape the geometry of networks with coarser representations. In both cases, the alignment results in improved downstream performance of the target network. Ultimately, this demonstrates that a model's architectural destiny can be decoupled from its physical structure and explicitly modified at initialization.
articles.title_zh: 传输架构为优化前置

articles.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Multi-UAV Data Harvesting Under Variable Team Sizes and Agent Loss
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collecting data from wireless sensors can be challenging when limited communication infrastructure prevents them from offloading their measurements. In such settings, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can exploit their mobility to harvest data locally, while coordinated UAV teams can provide efficient and redundant coverage of remote areas. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) enables such teams to learn decentralized coordination policies. However, training separate policies for different team and sensor populations is costly, and fixed-population policies may be vulnerable to agent failures. This work proposes F-MADDPG, a flexible variant of Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) that supports data harvesting with varying numbers of wireless sensors and UAVs. The framework also accommodates unexpected catastrophic failures that permanently remove agents during a mission. We compare F-MADDPG with a MADDPG baseline that uses multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) and evaluate training strategies based on team-size sampling and exposure to agent terminations. The results show that F-MADDPG learns across the evaluated population sizes, completes missions faster than the baseline on average, benefits from inverse-cardinality team-size sampling compared with uniform sampling, remains effective after permanent agent losses, and gains no consistent benefit from exposure to failures during training.
articles.title_zh: 在可变团队规模和代理损失下进行多UAV数据采集的深度强化学习

articles.title: Routeability Before Routing: Routeability Audit Protocol (RAP) and RouteabilityBench for Audited LLM Model Selection
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM routing aims to choose, for each prompt, which model in a portfolio is most likely to answer correctly. This only makes sense when the benchmark contains enough prompt-specific variation for different models to be best on different inputs. On coarse-scored LLM benchmarks, however, many models often tie for the best score, and the single best model may already leave little room for improvement. We therefore propose a routeability-first audit, instantiated as RAP and RouteabilityBench, a runnable claim-verification package. The audit is retrospective: it runs once the benchmark-portfolio score matrix exists and before router comparisons are interpreted as general evidence, rather than certifying a portfolio that has not yet been evaluated. Across four benchmarks and 66 LLMs, generic routing enhancements such as larger embedding sets, dimensionality reduction, selective abstention, clustering, and stronger regressors do not consistently outperform the single best model. The clearest positive evidence is concentrated in portfolio-dependent Omni-MATH settings, while GPQA, MMLU-Pro, and IFEval show different ways in which routing can remain hard or predictor-sensitive. Our practical recommendation is that routing gains should be reported together with routeability diagnostics, tied-best analysis, portfolio construction details, and family-corrected statistical tests.
articles.title_zh: 运行前的路由:路由审计协议(RAP)和经过审计的LLM模型选择的路由底板

articles.title: Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution. Executed actions, or decisions, taken in this manner are only as reliable as the model's predictive capabilities, and predictions in turn are only reliable within the model's experience. Epistemic uncertainty (EU) is the signal that marks where that experience ends. In this work we offer an extensive empirical study on how training objectives and architectures shape epistemic uncertainty of world models. More precisely, we present a controlled comparison of post-hoc EU (last-layer Laplace and ensembles) between two dominant models of different paradigms: 1) LeWorldModel (LeWM): A joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), which predicts the next embedding without a decoder, and 2) DreamerV3: A recurrent state-space model (RSSM), which reconstructs the observation from a recurrent latent state. In ten simulated visual-control environments, we follow a controlled state perturbation of the environment state through every stage of the models up to the final EU estimate. We find that the RSSM attenuates the state perturbation through two mechanisms before it reaches an estimator on the predictor feature. Its recurrent update averages over context, so a change in a single frame reaches the state at a fraction of its size and recovers only as the change persists. Its reconstruction objective weights an entity by the pixels it covers, so a small object can be lost due to the training objective. The JEPA has neither mechanism and passes the change through all stages to the uncertainty. We further show that this translates to gaps in five uncertainty related downstream tasks, from unfamiliar-state detection to uncertainty-penalised planning: the RSSM uncertainty misses deviations that its own posterior registers, whereas the JEPA uncertainty reports what its model sees.
articles.title_zh: 并非所有的世界模型都能够怀疑:培训目标和建筑如何影响JEPA和RSSM世界模型的认知不确定性

articles.title: Provably Efficient Offline Discounted Reinforcement Learning under Recursive Entropic Risk
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study risk-sensitive reinforcement learning in finite discounted infinite-horizon Markov Decision Processes with recursive entropic risk measures (ERM), parameterized by $\beta\neq 0$. We consider both risk-averse ($\beta>0$) and risk-seeking ($\beta<0$) settings. We consider the offline RL setting, where the agent is provided with a fixed dataset and wishes to learn a near-optimal policy using this dataset. We introduce a model-based algorithm, called ERM Value Iteration Lower Confidence Bound (ERM-VI-LCB) and derive a PAC-type bound on its sample complexity. We also establish a corresponding lower bound, demonstrating that exponential dependence on $|\beta|/(1-\gamma)$ asserted by the upper bound is unavoidable in the worst case. The presented bounds provide the first rigorous sample complexity guarantees for offline RL under recursive ERM across both risk-averse and risk-seeking regimes.
articles.title_zh: 在递归性环境风险下证明有效的离线贴现强化学习

articles.title: Put the World Back: Timestamps Matter in Time Series Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to time series reasoning. However, current evaluations often give models events in chronological order and already matched to the time series. This makes it unclear whether models use timestamps to connect events with observations or simply take shortcuts. To expose this ambiguity, we reformulate time series reasoning from a world-to-series projection perspective, viewing timestamps as explicit indices that connect numerical observations and external events to shared world states. We identify three structures that timestamps can make explicit: temporal causal structure, time semantics, and event-series alignment. Building on this perspective, we develop a diagnostic protocol that distinguishes timestamp-grounded reasoning from correlational shortcuts, a distinction that accuracy-based benchmarks cannot make. Controlled interventions on 310 questions from two tasks show that high accuracy can persist when timestamps are replaced by relative offsets or removed, while breaking event-series alignment induces systematic failures. When context is pre-aligned, models barely need timestamps. When order is missing, they use dates to recall world knowledge. Without dates, they rely on correlational shortcuts and rarely notice incorrect timestamps. These findings show that high accuracy on pre-aligned, ordered inputs does not establish that a model uses timestamps to synchronize observations with the world. We release our code, model outputs, and trajectory labels at https://github.com/tingrui-huang/timestamps-matter.
articles.title_zh: 把世界放回去:时间戳在时间序列中很重要

articles.title: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.34930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image model (0.299--0.371 \vs 0.214--0.232), and paired tests separate three tiers among the pathology models. Unlike a supervised probe, BioScore needs no labels, builds its reference from the data and scores even from few sections, yet it ranks the encoders as a probe does. Its per-identity breakdown indicates which cell identities each encoder captures or misses.
articles.title_zh: 病理学基础模型生物编码的基因知情基准

articles.title: Generalizable Equivariant Diffusion Models for Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory: Analytical Foundations and Numerical Scaling Tests
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.03530v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gauge-equivariant diffusion models can be used to generate ensembles of field configurations in non-abelian lattice gauge theories. Previously, we demonstrated the feasibility of modeling these theories by combining L-CNN-based diffusion models with the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA). Here we focus on the underlying analytical framework. In particular, we present a rigorous derivation of the reverse-time stochastic differential equation on the group manifold, discuss the gauge invariance of the denoising loss function, and provide extensive numerical benchmarks regarding the scaling behavior with respect to the lattice volume and the inverse coupling $\beta$. Full analytical expressions for arbitrarily sized Wilson loops and the topological charge susceptibility during the forward process are given as well.
articles.title_zh: 非阿贝利亚拉蒂斯·高格理论通用等效扩散模型:分析基础和数值放大测试

articles.title: The Symmetry Budget: How Much Group Structure Should a Network Architecture Assume?
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A network architecture is, in large part, a symmetry assumption: convolution ties weights across translations, attention ties them across permutations, and a fully connected layer ties nothing. When the data are only approximately symmetric, tying trades approximation error against estimation error, and the right amount of tying is a property of the dataset, not of the architecture alone. We study this trade-off in an exactly solvable model: linear maps on signals over the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_d$, with architectures indexed by the subgroup lattice of $\mathbb{Z}_d$, so that a single integer $k \mid d$ interpolates between an unconstrained layer ($k=1$, $d^2$ parameters) and a fully equivariant one ($k=d$, $d$ parameters). We derive the finite-sample excess risk in closed form, show that for a generic symmetry defect the leading-order risk is affine in $1/k$, and prove that intermediate architectures are then never strictly optimal: the lattice collapses to an all-or-nothing choice with phase boundary $n^\star = \sigma^2 d(d-1)/\varepsilon^2$. Structured defects break this collapse and restore interior optima, and we give a closed-form defect profile for a graded defect. Measurements agree with the theory on $60/60$ cells of a $(\varepsilon,n)$ phase diagram and $48/48$ cells of a second phase diagram at $d=16$, recover the predicted exponent as $-1.92$ against $-2$, and exhibit the predicted $k^\star: 12 \to 4 \to 1$ ladder under graded defects; a two-layer nonlinear control reproduces the crossover. We also characterize when the affine collapse survives for non-abelian groups.
articles.title_zh: 对称预算:一个网络结构应该有多大?

articles.title: One Neural Operator for Re-planning Low-Thrust Cislunar Transfers after Thrust Outages, at the Original or a Later Arrival
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Safe-mode events causing thrust outages are common in missions with electric propulsion. To demonstrate mission feasibility in such an event, missed-thrust margin studies are performed where thousands of outage scenarios need an exact re-plan solved. We train a neural operator that maps a nominal trajectory with an outage profile to a re-planned trajectory and to the probability that the recovery exists, for 270 low-thrust near-rectilinear halo orbit (NRHO) to distant retrograde orbit (DRO) transfers, at an allowed slip of up to 10 days. On unseen transfers and zero slip, its median control error on the severe half of outages is 1.20% compared to 14.0% for the best cheap re-planner benchmark. With the arrival slip as an input, the error is 1.67% against 23.2%. It also predicts the recoverability of an outage for a given arrival slip with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.997, while the minimum recoverable slip prediction is optimistic by more than half a day on only 6 of the 84 checked outages needing slip. At the original arrival, the ensemble spread of an operator variant with solver inputs has a rank correlation of 0.91 with the actual error, and performing exact solves on the 31% most uncertain severe outages reduces the 90th-percentile error from 8.5% to 2.3%. A query takes milliseconds without a solver, making this a useful tool for large outage studies where the cost of thousands of exact solves outweighs the time to train the operator.
articles.title_zh: 一个神经操作员,用于在断流后重新规划低振荡的西斯卢纳转动,时间为原始时间或稍后到达时间

articles.title: A Causal Energy Prior for Learning Directed Acyclic Graphs
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayesian learning of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) has long relied on non- or weakly informative priors, on the assumption that the information needed for an informative one is rarely available. In genetics and systems biology, annotation databases now make it possible to assemble a prior DAG before learning from data. Existing informative priors are local: they score a DAG arc by arc and cannot encode how interventions propagate along its paths. Thus, we propose the local-global energy prior (LGE), a Gibbs distribution over DAGs whose energy combines a local divergence from the prior DAG, the Structural Hamming Distance, and a causal one, the Structural Intervention Distance. We derive rules to calibrate its decay and the weight of the two divergences from the prior DAG alone. We quantify how much prior mass stays on the true DAG, and how much data overturn the prior, when the prior DAG is partially incorrect. In simulations, LGE improves both the structural accuracy of maximum a posteriori DAGs and the fit of the corresponding Bayesian networks to the true distribution over non- and weakly informative priors, even when half of the arcs of the prior DAG are wrong. We also showcase LGE on a gene regulatory network learned from single-cell kidney data.
articles.title_zh: 学习前因果能源

articles.title: Real Package, Wrong Controller: Static Auditing of Vendor--Protocol Mismatches in LLM-Generated PLC Code
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models can generate Python that drives industrial protocols on programmable logic controllers, yet existing code-grounding checks ask whether an imported package or symbol exists rather than whether it suits the declared industrial target. We define \emph{metadata-conditioned, import-level vendor--protocol incompatibility} and build \textsc{Proteus-OT}, a label-free static verifier over a version-pinned graph of documented bindings. Across 883 generated scripts, 180 carry an import-level mismatch against the declared target (20.4\%); restricting to single-vendor targets gives 16.3\%, and additionally requiring the offending library to reach a protocol communication call gives 14.2\%, which we read as conditional on the corpus metadata rather than on verified intent. None of the 28 adjudicable human control files carries one, a sample too small to estimate a prevalence. Within the balanced subset, 96.6\% of mismatching scripts import packages and call methods that exist, so an existence baseline does not represent them, and every positive ships with an inspectable witness. We also audit machine-versus-human classification on the same corpus, where character $n$-grams reach macro-F1 1.000 under task, model and vendor-disjoint partitions and survive comment removal, an AST round trip and identifier anonymisation. The trailing newline present in 95.2\% of human files and in none of the generated ones separates the classes on its own. Vendor--protocol consistency is a useful static audit target, whereas provenance classification on repository-labelled corpora is not authorship detection.
articles.title_zh: Real 套件, 错误控制器: LLM- Geneded PLC 代码中的供应商协议错误的静态审计

articles.title: Effect-Driven Skill Abstractions for Offline Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We seek to learn discrete skill abstractions to facilitate long-horizon, goal-conditioned reinforcement-learning (RL) tasks. Recent approaches have shown success by quantizing actions via clustering or reconstruction. However, these objectives lead to skills that are not directly related to what the current state affords or what the goal requires. Instead, we argue that goal-directed skills should be driven by \emph{how they affect the state} of the agent. To realize this, we introduce a novel quantization method for action chunks that optimizes next-state predictions conditioned on the current state and action. This objective encourages skills to be distinguished by the future states they lead to, resulting in a vocabulary that spans diverse outcomes reachable from a given state. Our framework can easily be paired with common offline RL methods by replacing their continuous actor head with a discrete one that selects among the learned skills. We can execute these skills in the environment by converting them back to continuous actions using a trained low-level controller. Experiments on benchmark navigation and manipulation tasks largely show substantial and consistent improvements over both the continuous-actor baselines and reconstruction-based discretizations. Our project page can be found at: https://burcukilic.github.io/projects/effect-driven-skill-abstractions/.
articles.title_zh: 离线强化学习效果驱动技能摘要

articles.title: MonoQPM: Splitting Features into Concepts for Inherent Interpretability and Predictive Performance
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alongside superposition, polysemanticity is one of the primary obstacles to achieving interpretable deep neural networks. While these phenomena are typically intrinsically linked, the Quadratic Programming Enhanced Model (QPM) naturally decouples them. By representing classes with a sparse binary assignment of very few features, QPM prevents superposition by design on its final features but still exhibits polysemanticity. However, measuring polysemanticity is an open problem. This work proposes a utility-focused approach to measuring polysemanticity by quantifying the decrease in interference-induced activation errors, which yields the practical utility of tighter prediction sets using Conformal Prediction (CP). We explicitly disentangle the polysemantic features of QPM into monosemantic concepts to create the Monosemantic QPM (MonoQPM). Because its features are disentangled, MonoQPM acts as a significantly more efficient Conformal Predictor. Additionally, we introduce CUBCars, a dataset providing ground truth information about shared concepts. Using this and other datasets, we demonstrate that polysemanticity emerges in QPM across all tested architectures, but is effectively alleviated by MonoQPM. For instance, MonoQPM guarantees 88% coverage using Adaptive Prediction Sets on ImageNet with just 66% of the frozen QPM's set size.
articles.title_zh: Mono QPM: 将特性分为内在解释和预测性能的概念

articles.title: Same Tokenizer, Better Tokens: Choosing Image Tokens by MAP Inference
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete visual tokens encode images for reconstruction and serve as training targets for autoregressive image generators. Vector-quantized tokenizers typically assign each encoder feature its nearest code independently. The decoder uses these codes jointly, so a sequence of individually nearest codes can reconstruct an image less faithfully than an alternative assignment. A local model of the reconstruction loss yields a closest-vector problem with a decoder-dependent target and metric. Reconstruction-only search improves PSNR across the frozen tokenizers we test. Different code sequences can achieve similar reconstruction quality, leaving room to favour more predictable ones. We introduce RecaP (Reconstruction and Predictability), which selects codes for a frozen tokenizer by balancing how faithfully they reconstruct the image with how likely their sequence is under a pretrained autoregressive prior. On ImageNet, LlamaGen GPT-B trained on RecaP tokens achieves lower early-checkpoint FID against training images than GPT-B trained on nearest-neighbour tokens. The difference is smaller against held-out images. On an ImageNet subset, the prior improves generation at comparable reconstruction FID. Our code is available at: https://github.com/gmum/recap
articles.title_zh: 相同的托肯泽尔,更好的托肯斯:通过MAP推论选择图像托肯斯

articles.title: JetDiffusion: Pushing the Speed Limits of Video Generation with NVFP4 Sparse Attention
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attention over long sequences is a major computational bottleneck in video generation, which can be alleviated through sparsity and low-bit quantization. We propose JetDiffusion, a video generation system built on trainable Video Sparse Quantized Attention (VSQA), with custom inference kernels that combine native NVFP4 computation and kernel fusion. At 90% sparsity, VSQA accelerates attention by 8-29x compared with FlashAttention on different hardwares. To further accelerate video generation, we combine VSQA with NVFP4 linear quantization and step distillation. Although each technique can individually preserve generation quality, jointly adapting to all three remains challenging, particularly under aggressive NVFP4 quantization. Through empirical studies, we develop an effective staged training recipe that enables stable adaptation to quantization, sparsity, and few-step denoising. On Wan2.1-14B, the resulting model achieves 273x end-to-end video generation speedup on the RTX 5090 while maintaining comparable video quality.
articles.title_zh: JetDifusion:用NVFP4 Sparse 注意推进视频生成速度限制

articles.title: Large-scale Model Merging via Recovery-aware Task Weighting
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model merging combines multiple task-specific expert models into a single model. However, merging preserves expert capabilities unevenly across tasks. This imbalance is particularly pronounced in large-scale settings, where some tasks can suffer severe capability losses even when average accuracy remains high. To address this imbalance, we introduce Recovery-aware Task Weighting (RaTW), a model merging framework that assigns larger weights to tasks whose expert capabilities are poorly retained by an initial merged model. We quantify these recovery opportunities as the fraction of a task's labeled validation samples that its expert predicts correctly but the initial merged model gets wrong, and use the resulting task weights to re-merge the experts. To evaluate merging at large scale, we construct CLIPMerge-100, a 100-task benchmark with task-specific experts on CLIP ViT-L/14 and ViT-B/32. Across eleven merging methods with 20, 50, and 100 tasks on two CLIP backbones, RaTW improves both mean accuracy and tail20 (the mean expert-normalized accuracy of the 20% worst-retained tasks) in all 33 ViT-L/14 settings and 32 of 33 ViT-B/32 settings. We further introduce ReForge++, which combines RaTW with iterative model refinement and outperforms all evaluated baselines, including a matched-budget control, in both mean accuracy and tail20 across all settings.
articles.title_zh: 通过认识到回收任务加权进行大规模模型合并

articles.title: What Does RL Post-Training Teach Text-to-Image Models? A Skill-Wise Analysis of Flow-GRPO
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has become a standard way to improve text-to-image flow models: Flow-GRPO lifts the GenEval score of SD3.5-M from 0.63 to 0.95, a gain read as the model having learned compositional generation. We ask how much of that gain the base model's own samples already contained, by measuring pass@k over shared noise seeds, one skill at a time, before and after RL, on prompts never used in training. The answer differs by skill. On four of GenEval's six skills, where 32 base samples already solve almost every prompt, the gain is sharpening: one post-trained sample is worth 4 to 10 base samples, and pass@32 barely moves. On spatial relations it is unlocking: pass@32 rises from 0.69 to 1.00, 128 base samples do not match one post-trained sample, and prompts the base model never solved in 32 samples are solved 93% of the time, as often as those it solved. The benchmark average, 31 base samples per post-trained sample, describes no skill. Relations carry 35% of the gain; of the other 65%, selecting among 8 base samples with the judge behind the reward recovers nine tenths. We propose an account of when each occurs: within a prompt, a group-relative update re-weights only the outcomes its samples contain, and a flow policy cannot widen the noise that produces them; across prompts, shared parameters let successes on some prompts repair a deficit common to many. The same anatomy applies to a text-rendering checkpoint. The account's predictions are tested with a checkpoint trained without KL, within-prompt diversity, and controlled training that holds object classes out, where sharpening comes first and transfers, and unlocking follows, on practised objects before unseen ones.
articles.title_zh: RL 后培训教学文本到图像模型是什么? 流动技能分析

articles.title: What Must LLM Agents Communicate? From Information Loss to Communication Failures
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33318v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When evidence is distributed across LLM agents, a team may collectively possess all the information needed for a decision yet fail to use it effectively. What must agents communicate for accurate joint predictions, and when does interaction help? We study three requirements for effective communication: sufficiency of the information conveyed, selection of relevant evidence, and utilization of received information. Drawing on information theory and communication complexity, we develop a framework that combines theoretical benchmarks with controlled experiments and message-level analyses. We find that local probability reports can discard essential information, with theoretical information loss closely matching observed performance penalties. Query-first interaction improves predictions when relevant evidence depends on a private query, but compact one-shot representations can eliminate this advantage. Even when sufficient information is communicated, agents may fail to select or use it correctly. Together, these findings distinguish fundamental communication limits from failures in how LLM agents communicate and use information.
articles.title_zh: LLM智能体必须沟通什么? 从信息损失到通信故障

articles.title: Evaluating Ensemble Methods for Algorithmic Stability Under Data Perturbations
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard classification algorithms often exhibit sensitivity near decision boundaries, which can compound instability that already exists from overfitting to a subset of high-influence samples. Ensembling is commonly used to stabilize classifiers, but we show that it can destabilize those that are already stable. The well-established practice of subbagging can yield substantial improvements in stability, as we validate in the cause-of-death classification setting. However, its effect depends on the perturbation level, and for stable classifiers the finite number of bags introduces destabilizing Monte Carlo noise that shrinks only slowly as the number of bags grows. This instability can be mitigated, though, by the recently proposed inflated argmax, which allows for multi-class predictions in ambiguous cases. We further examine the extent to which the Rashomon set, the collection of distinct models that achieve near-optimal predictive performance, can reduce instability by leveraging predictive multiplicity rather than resampling. We find that the Rashomon ensemble can stabilize unstable classifiers, but requires sufficient predictive multiplicity, which is not guaranteed. It is a promising direction, but not currently a general substitute for subbagging. Our results are consistent with an influence equalization interpretation of why these ensemble approaches stabilize unstable classifiers, although their failures on stable classifiers appear to have distinct sources.
articles.title_zh: 评估数据扰动下的算法稳定性方法

articles.title: Probabilistic Machine Learning for Total Kinetic Energy Distributions in Neutron-Induced Fission
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The incident-neutron-energy dependence of post-neutron total-kinetic-energy (TKE) distributions, particularly their width in the multichance-fission regime, provides a sensitive test of fission calculations. We investigate how the General Description of Fission Observables (GEF) and probabilistic machine-learning models trained on GEF reproduce measured TKE distributions, emphasizing their width at high incident-neutron energies and extrapolation beyond the training range. Gaussian process regression (GPR), GPR with a white-noise kernel, a mixture density network (MDN), and a Bayesian mixture density network (BMDN) are evaluated on a common calculated dataset. An extended MDN/BMDN analysis uses 1,025 GEF spectra from 20 target nuclei and 60 measured distributions. Training ranges of up to 20, 40, and approximately 76 MeV are compared with matched-size controls extending to 30 or 40 MeV while preserving the number of spectra per target. Above 40 MeV, the BMDN width mean absolute error relative to experiment decreases from 5.63 MeV for training up to 20 MeV to 2.70 and 2.53 MeV for two matched-size 30-MeV controls and 1.77 MeV for the matched-size 40-MeV control. Predictive-interval coverage relative to GEF above 40 MeV rises from 52.3% to 92.3% between the 20-MeV and full training ranges. Agreement with measured mean TKE and widths is target dependent, with no uniform ordering among GEF, MDN, and BMDN. The results demonstrate the sensitivity of high-energy widths to training-energy coverage, with improvements already evident at 30 MeV. The comparatively slow variation of GEF widths at high energies limits the extent to which these improvements can be attributed to learning nontrivial energy dependence. Adequate training-energy coverage is critical for reproducing the calculated high-energy evolution, while agreement with experiment remains constrained by the underlying fission model.
articles.title_zh: 中子诱导的机能分配总量的概率机器学习

articles.title: Can a Short Video Clip Verify a Model Fix?
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33393v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A developer who reproduces a video model's error on a short clip can replay that clip after an update. How often does a correct clip answer mean the original test now passes? On 960 prespecified CG-Bench questions, we updated from Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct to Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct. Accuracy on a 64-frame sample spanning the full video rose from 27.9% to 33.3%. Before scoring the newer model, we froze 388 clips on which the older model reproduced its exact reference error. The updated model passed the reference on 51 of 116 clip passes (44.0%, 95% Wilson interval 35.3-53.0%) and on 16 of 272 clip failures (5.9%). Closing cases on a clip pass would have declared 65 unresolved reference failures fixed. Requiring a clip pass would have missed 16 of the 67 reference fixes (23.9%). In a separate 1,028-video study with different checkpoints and direct option scoring, only 15 clips passed, and the 16-frame reference confirmed one. For the generated-answer update, the short replay identified cases worth checking, while the original input remained necessary to verify individual fixes.
articles.title_zh: 一个短视频剪贴可以校验一个模型修饰吗 ?

articles.title: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Pursuit Game for Locomotor Agility Pretraining
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33407v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agile humanoid locomotion requires controllers that can adapt to rapidly changing motion demands while remaining stable and robust. Recent locomotion controllers are typically designed with either a dense reward that is carefully shaped to encourage steps and penalize falling, or by using a reference tracking reward which teaches the controller to follow predetermined motions. Once a behavior that maximizes the reward is discovered, the controller ceases to learn. While generally stable, reference tracking methods focus on motor control separately from motion generation. Self-play has been proven as an effective technique for superhuman performance on several multiagent games like Go, Starcraft, hide-and-seek, and capture-the-flag. We train neural networks to play the game of multiagent tag in a physics simulator to study if new motion generation and control strategies can emerge through sparse feedback and competitive self-play. We present MJTag, a task suite for role-conditioned locomotion during competitive pursuit-evasion. Our model is a role-conditioned policy for a low-level locomotion controller and optional planar velocity commands. MJTag's league-based play with sparse feedback enables a locomotion controller to adopt new strategies, including dodging, sprinting, and tackling.
articles.title_zh: 为 Locomotor Acility Pretrain 制作的对等多代理游戏

articles.title: ViCARD: Visual Credit Assignment with Reward-Gated Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual reasoning requires models to identify relevant visual evidence and use it to derive correct answers. Outcomebased reinforcement learning (RL) faces two key challenges in this regime: it yields no learning signal when perceptual errors cause all sampled responses to fail, and it broadcasts a uniform advantage across every token within a response. Conversely, while visual self-distillation offers dense guidance from evidence-centered image crops, student learning from token distributions alone often fails to elicit correct final answers. Motivated by an audit of training rollouts that exposes these complementary failure modes, we introduce ViCARD (Visual Credit Assignment with RewardGated Distillation), which integrates per-token visual supervision with verified correctness rewards. For each rollout group, we leverage a teacher with its input image cropped to the relevant visual area, and use this to provide per-token supervision to the student while also valuing correctness. If all sampled rollouts fail, ViCARD samples an additional crop-teacher answer and activates on-policy distillation only if that answer is correct. Together, these mechanisms provide fine-grained visual credit within informative reward groups and a learning signal for otherwise uninformative all-fail groups. Extensive comparisons across model scales demonstrate that ViCARD improves fine-grained visual reasoning performance over RL and distillation baselines, while retaining broad visual reasoning capabilities.
articles.title_zh: ViCARD:可视化信贷转让,为多种方式提供有偿的蒸馏

articles.title: Centered Kernel Distance: Dimension-Free Error Bounds for Comparing Neural Representations
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The asymptotic error of representational similarity metrics such as centered kernel alignment (CKA) and representational similarity analysis (RSA) has been well-characterized, but there are no realistic bounds on how estimates of representational similarity $\textit{simultaneously}$ depend on the number of sampled neurons ($N$) and experimental conditions ($M$). We study the natural metric counterpart of CKA and RSA, which we call the Centered Kernel Distance (CKD). We show that CKD admits an unbiased estimator, whereas several popular similarity measures including CKA have no unbiased estimator. Under mild assumptions, we show that estimation error of CKD decays in proportion to $1/M + 1/N$. Strikingly, the rate in this bound does not depend on the dimensionality of the space of experimental conditions. Thus, similarity estimation does not suffer from the curse of dimensionality, which plagues similar problems in high-dimensional statistics. We verify our results empirically in random shallow neural networks, trained neural networks, and macaque visual cortex data. Ultimately, this paper advances a framework for predicting the error of similarity estimators in experiments by relaxing existing, biologically-unrealistic assumptions. Our theoretical and empirical predictions produce specific prescriptions on how to most efficiently estimate the similarity between multiple neural systems.
articles.title_zh: 中心内核距离:用于比较神经表达的无尺寸错误

articles.title: A Realistic End-to-End Runtime Crossover Estimation for Quantum-Enhanced Training of Large-Scale Machine Learning Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine Learning (ML) is one promising application domain for Quantum Computing (QC) speedups, but asymptotic complexity considerations often mask the actual engineering costs of actual end-to-end workflows. For the use case of training a linearized Neural Network with a Quantum Linear Solver, a provably favorable quantum scaling has been suggested. We present realistic resource estimates for this problem, accounting for data access, computation, and readout. Our analysis examines three increasingly complex benchmarking scenarios, under distinct sparsity-scaling assumptions, thereby enabling progressively more realistic resource estimates. We identify crossover regimes relative to classical methods and find that crossover points emerge only for very large problem sizes, long computation times, and highly restrictive output requirements. This work provides a blueprint for evaluating quantum-enhanced ML algorithms under realistic hardware constraints and help identifying the bottlenecks that must be overcome to approach industrial quantum utility.
articles.title_zh: 大规模机器学习模式量子强化培训的实事求是的终到末运行时间交叉估计

articles.title: SplatWAM: Splatting World Action Models for Real-Time 3D Imagination
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models typically predict future observations in pixel or latent space, limiting their ability to directly represent true 3D scene evolution. We present SplatWAM (Splatting World Action Model), a generative world model that learns action-conditioned dynamics directly over compact 3D Gaussian primitives. A tokenizer SplatWAM-T first encodes a variable number of unposed views into a fixed budget of Gaussian tokens. A dynamics model SplatWAM-D then predicts future Gaussian states in a single forward pass per action, using log-Euclidean covariance coordinates and differentiable rendering supervision to facilitate learning in an explicit 3D space. Each predicted state can be rasterized from arbitrary viewpoints, enforcing a shared 3D representation across views by construction. On OGBench Scene, SplatWAM renders novel views 12x faster than video world models (~80 FPS on an RTX 5090) with up to 2.0 dB higher PSNR. We further introduce SplatWAM-P, a lightweight flow-matching policy head jointly trained with the dynamics model. Across 8 task suites, model-free Gaussian-token policies outperform pixel-based counterparts by up to 24.8 percentage points. SplatWAM-P improves over Latent Particle World Model (LPWM) by 12 percentage points and matches HIQL without a learned value function. On LIBERO, our ~1B model outperforms WorldVLA (~7B) and the robot-pretrained OpenVLA (~7B), while matching OpenVLA-OFT when both are trained without large-scale robot pretraining. Code and checkpoints will be released.
articles.title_zh: SplateWAM:为实时三维想象而翻版的世界行动模型

articles.title: A comprehensive survey of deep face verification systems adversarial attacks and defense strategies
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Face Verification (FV) systems have exhibited remarkable performance in verification tasks and have consequently garnered extensive adoption across various applications, from identity duplication to authentication in mobile payments. However, the surge in popularity of face verification has raised concerns about potential vulnerabilities in the face of adversarial attacks. These concerns originate from the fact that advanced FV systems, which rely on deep neural networks, have recently demonstrated susceptibility to crafted input samples known as adversarial examples. Although imperceptible to human observers, adversarial examples can deceive deep neural networks during the testing and deployment phases. These vulnerabilities raised significant concerns about the deployment of deep neural networks in safety-critical contexts, prompting extensive investigations into adversarial attacks and corresponding defense strategies. This comprehensive survey provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in deep face verification, encompassing a broad spectrum of topics such as algorithmic designs, database utilization, protocols, and application scenarios. Furthermore, we conduct an in-depth examination of state-of-the-art algorithms to generate adversarial examples and the defense mechanisms devised to mitigate such adversarial threats.
articles.title_zh: 全面调查面部深层核查制度、对抗攻击和防御战略

articles.title: StyleID++: Position-Decoupled and Structure-Coherent Style Retrieval across Diffusion Architectures
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attention injection offers a remarkably simple route to training-free style transfer: content queries retrieve style keys and values inside a pretrained diffusion model. We show that this operation also creates an overlooked failure mode. Position signals that are useful within one image become a spurious shared coordinate system across two spatially unrelated images, causing content tokens to favor style tokens at similar coordinates. This cross-image positional leakage appears in both convolutional U-Nets and diffusion transformers (DiTs), despite their different position mechanisms. Removing the positional shortcut exposes a second problem: unconstrained global retrieval lets related content tokens select incompatible style regions, producing fragmented appearance. We present StyleID++, a training-free framework that addresses the two problems jointly. Position-Decoupled Retrieval reduces coordinate-dependent matching through circular padding in U-Nets and injection-only RoPE removal in DiTs, while preserving native position modeling elsewhere. Affinity-Coherent Refinement then regularizes style assignments with the content self-attention graph, encouraging structurally related tokens to retrieve compatible style evidence. We quantify the leakage with a coordinate--centroid correlation and a permutation test on the style reference. The permutation error can be driven to zero in both backbones, which identifies the position mechanism as the carrier of the leakage, and StyleID++ obtains the best ArtFID of all methods we compare.
articles.title_zh: StyleID ++: 位置解析和结构解析

articles.title: LGCount: Layout-Guided Diffusion for Zero-Shot Object Counting
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33344v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Class-agnostic counting requires the user to specify what to count, usually with a class name or a few annotated boxes. We propose a richer text-based specification: a structured layout that names the target, the region that holds it, the distractors to ignore. A prompt upsampler writes this layout from the image and the requested category alone, and an image-editing diffusion model, adapted into a single-step counter, turns it into a density map. Because counting datasets pair each image with a single valid density map, a counter trained on it learns to ignore the layout. We therefore train on synthetic counterfactuals in which one image admits several valid density maps, so that the layout cannot be ignored. On FSC-147 we improve on the previous zero-shot state of the art and we set the best reported result on LOOKALIKES while being told the least about each image. A single photograph can be counted by category, by region, or by granularity without retraining.
articles.title_zh: LGCount: 零热对象计数的布局引导扩散

articles.title: Searching Ultra-Long Videos with Decision Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding ultra-long videos requires retrieving sparse, query-relevant evidence from extensive video histories. Existing similarity-based retrieval methods are efficient, but they encode the question and the video content independently and thus often miss evidence whose relevance requires reasoning over both. Generative large language models (LLMs) can perform such reasoning, but they typically generate text over multiple rounds of search, which makes each query slow and costly. In this work, we introduce DeLoVi (Decision Models for Long Video), a framework that leverages pretrained decision models to retrieve evidence from ultra-long videos. Like an LLM, a decision model reads the question together with the candidate evidence, so it can reason over both. Unlike an LLM, it directly outputs a relevance score without generating text, which makes it fast and inexpensive. We first present DeLoVi-S, a simple method that generates captions for short video clips and uses a decision model to rank those captions by their relevance to a question. A generative LLM then answers the question using the top-ranked captions. Despite its simplicity, DeLoVi-S achieves state-of-the-art performance on three ultra-long video understanding benchmarks, EgoLifeQA, EgoMemReason, and MM-Lifelong, and generalizes effectively to long-video understanding benchmarks, VideoMME-L and LVBench. However, DeLoVi-S scores every caption for every question, so its cost grows linearly with video length. To reduce this cost, we propose an automated policy evolution framework that iteratively refines the memory construction and retrieval policies around a fixed pretrained decision model. The resulting method, DeLoVi-E, maintains comparable performance while reducing input tokens by 34x on average compared with DeLoVi-S. It also runs over 3x faster than the best prior method on EgoLifeQA while achieving higher accuracy.
articles.title_zh: 以决定模式搜索超长视频

articles.title: MotifFlow: Training-Free, Self-Contained Style Transfer from Color to Motif in Rectified Flow Transformers
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Expressive style transfer must reproduce a painting's palette, brushwork, and characteristic motifs while retaining the content image's structure. Attention injection is effective in U-Net-based diffusion models, but adapting it to FLUX often transfers color without capturing the style's distinctive brushwork. Our analysis across backbones links this gap to how injected features are integrated across neighboring spatial locations. We introduce MotifFlow, a training-free, self-contained framework that combines style injection with style-alignment guidance in FLUX. Injection supplies style features during generation but does not explicitly encourage the model's native attention output to align with them. We therefore use the discrepancy between native and injected attention outputs to guide latent-space updates, encouraging the evolving image to develop the style's distinctive brushwork and motifs. Style encoding, guidance, and synthesis all use the same frozen backbone, without auxiliary image encoders or trained adapters. A single strength parameter controls the transition from color transfer to pronounced brushwork and motifs, with additional support for regional stylization and style mixing. Experiments on 1,000 content-style pairs show that MotifFlow better matches the local textures of the style image than baseline methods and produces more consistent stylization than injection alone. The same design extends to FLUX.2.
articles.title_zh: MotifFlow: 校正流程变换器中从颜色到 Motif 的自定义样式传输

articles.title: Beyond Random Starts: Amortized Initialization for Adversarial Attacks on Vision-Language Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gradient-based transferable adversarial attacks achieve state-of-the-art attack success rates against black-box vision-language models (VLMs). However, they require hundreds of costly optimization steps for each image pair. One possible reason is that these attacks typically start from random perturbations that contain no information about the source or target image. In this work, we study whether amortized adversarial generation can provide better initializations for gradient-based attacks. By learning across many image pairs, amortization allows a generator to produce adversarial perturbations for new inputs without optimizing each perturbation from scratch. We introduce SPARK, a lightweight looped perturbation generator conditioned on both the source and target images. SPARK repeatedly applies the same network to refine a perturbation, producing effective adversarial attacks in a few forward passes without requiring gradients through surrogate vision encoders at inference time. We show that these perturbations provide effective warm starts for existing gradient-based attacks, substantially improving attack success rates while reducing the number of optimization steps required. These improvements generalize across different attack methods, VLMs, and unseen image categories. SPARK also produces effective standalone attacks at a fraction of the computational cost of gradient-based optimization. Code and model weights are available at https://github.com/Patchwork53/SPARK.
articles.title_zh: Beyond Random Starts:Aversarial 攻击视觉-语言模型的模拟初始化

articles.title: FoamSurf: A Voronoi-Surfel Representation for Differentiable Rendering
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scenes inside a scattering medium contain solid surfaces, such as the seabed or rocks, and a semi-transparent medium, such as water, fog, or smoke. Recent Gaussian-based methods produce realistic images of scenes in scattering media, but traces of the medium can remain visible in surface-only renders. Neural fields separate surfaces and medium more accurately, but they are slow to train and difficult to edit. Both approaches evaluate the medium only along camera rays, so its effects along reflected and refracted rays are not modeled. These limitations prevent reliable surface recovery, independent editing of surfaces and the medium, and consistent rendering of inserted objects. We present FoamSurf, a hybrid representation that models surfaces with planar Gaussian surfels and the medium with space-filling Voronoi cells. A single differentiable ray tracer composites both along arbitrary rays, while training priors keep them separate without segmentation masks. Across real underwater scenes, synthetic scenes, and dense fog, FoamSurf achieves image quality on par with the state of the art and the most accurate surface-medium separation among the compared methods. The recovered components can be removed, edited, or stylized independently, and the same reconstruction supports inserted mesh objects with attenuation and scattering along both direct and reflected or refracted rays. Together, these capabilities enable scene restoration, editing, and composition within a single reconstructed model. Project page: https://grzegorzwilczynski.com/foamsurf/
articles.title_zh: FoamSurf:用于不同渲染的Voroni-Surfel代表

articles.title: Memory as the Backbone: A Dual-Store Associative Memory Architecture for Visual Recognition
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether explicit memory can serve as the organizing principle of a general-purpose visual backbone. Inspired by the interaction between working and long-term memory in human cognition, we introduce DuSAM (Dual-Store Associative Memory), a hierarchical memory-native visual backbone coupling image-local working memory (WM) with a fixed-capacity persistent semantic memory (PM). WM organizes local visual evidence into compact, spatially anchored states that are updated and transported across stages, then read back to refine dense features. PM consolidates semantic evidence from training images and annotated regions into prototypes, whose retrieved content enriches the same working states. With these memory operations in place of self-attention or state-space blocks, DuSAM achieves competitive performance relative to representative, similarly sized backbones on ImageNet-1K classification, ADE20K semantic segmentation, and COCO object detection and instance segmentation. Ablations show contributions from both stores, with PM particularly benefiting class groups with fewer annotated training pixels. At $2048\times2048$, the complete DuSAM-based UPerNet segmentor achieves $2.36\times$ the throughput of the evaluated DeiT-S/16 counterpart while using $59.5\%$ less GPU memory, and $1.24\times$ the throughput of the linear-complexity VMamba-T. Memory analyses reveal spatially selective WM access and semantic associations between retrieved prototypes and training regions. Class-targeted removal and restoration further demonstrate that category-specific experience can be replenished through state updates without changing network parameters. These results establish explicit memory as a viable organizing principle for visual backbones and provide a foundation for jointly designing contextual computation and addressable semantic memory.
articles.title_zh: 记忆作为 Backbone: 视觉识别的双层关联记忆架构

articles.title: Separating Environment and Sensor Shift from Acquisition Protocol in Physical Vision Benchmarks
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In real-world deployments, vision systems must operate under varying environmental conditions, such as illumination changes. Recent work has explored adaptive sensing strategies that select camera parameters according to the current environment and downstream task to improve task performance. Reliable physical benchmarks are therefore essential for evaluating such strategies. We study ImageNet-ES-Diverse, a physical benchmark that evaluates the adaptive exposure control strategy Lens by recapturing printed ImageNet images under varying illumination conditions. We construct four controlled acquisition pipelines that vary printed-image scale and camera zoom, and conduct a pilot study with directly captured physical objects. We find that the acquisition choices substantially change benchmark difficulty on all downstream baselines. Moreover, the average classification-accuracy advantage of Lens over auto exposure observed on the original benchmark does not persist in either our collected pipelines or real-object pilot study. Oracle exposure selection nevertheless retains substantial gains, indicating remaining potential for sensor control. These findings highlight acquisition protocol as an important factor in physical benchmark evaluation and motivate explicit protocol reporting and evaluation across multiple acquisition setups when assessing adaptive-sensing benefits.
articles.title_zh: 将环境和传感器从实际愿景基准中的购置协议中分离出来

articles.title: AVERT: Anomalous Value Erasure with Response Testing against Visual Prompt Injection
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) are vulnerable to visual prompt injection, in which an adversarially perturbed image forces the model to respond with the attacker's chosen content, such as malicious tool calls, website links, or advertisements, sometimes regardless of the user's question. Existing defenses, such as diffusion-based purification and image-token masking, mitigate these attacks at a substantial cost to the model's utility on benign inputs. To address this challenge, we propose AVERT, which removes adversarial feature directions only when the model's answer depends on them. Our key procedures involve identifying anomalous value subspaces and detecting answer dependence. To identify the anomalous value subspace, we compare the statistics of each input's attention-head outputs with those of clean images and extract the directions along which the input deviates the most. We then project out these directions to remove the injected content. Because the same directions also carry benign visual information, we apply the removal only to answers that depend on them, namely answers whose likelihood collapses once the directions are removed or that are as likely under unrelated questions as under the user's question. Against white-box attacks on four VLMs (Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, LLaVA, InternVL2.5) and four injection benchmarks, AVERT lowers average attack success from 86-90% to at most 0.6% while retaining at least 96% of undefended utility averaged over thirteen benchmarks. Its defense-utility F-score ($F_{DU}$), the harmonic mean of attacks stopped and utility retained, is 98.0-99.1 and the highest among all compared defenses on every model.
articles.title_zh: AVERT:反常值与视觉快速注射反应测试

articles.title: ProPolar: Progressive Polar Decomposition for Implicit Neural Representations
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) capture global low-frequency structure during the early stage of training and then refine localized high-frequency details, afterwards. However, standard optimizers are agnostic to the coarse-to-fine learning behavior of INRs. Such optimizers accumulate a gradient matrix in momentum buffer and retain components misaligned with the dominant low-frequency directions in the early stage. We propose a progressively growing rank scheduler and a rank-aware learning-rate scheduler for enhancing a subspace-based momentum optimization, where a momentum matrix is updated within a low-rank subspace. The rank schedule expands the subspace during training, and the scheduler holds the peak learning rate through rank growth so that the added subspace contributes to fine-detail recovery. Experiments on image fitting, single-image super-resolution (SISR), and neural radiance field optimization show that the proposed method improves convergence and peak reconstruction quality over competitive optimizers. The largest gains appear in the high-frequency refinement stage, mirroring the coarse-to-fine progression that the rank schedule targets. A significant study on hyperparameter optimization (HPO) on NeRF further confirms that these gains persist under matched search budgets.
articles.title_zh: ProPolar:对隐性神经表现的渐进极分解

articles.title: LLMVC: Large Language Model-Guided Generative Video Compression
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent generative video methods achieve strong perceptual compression by encoding videos into compact latent representations and reconstructing them with powerful generative decoders. However, visual encoders must compress both high-level semantics and dense visual details into a unified latent space, which complicates entropy coding and decoding and may cause semantic drift under aggressive compression. In this work, we propose Large Language Model-Guided Video Compression (LLMVC), which leverages the summarization capability of frozen video large language models (Video-LLMs) to generate compact semantic tokens aligned with temporal latent slices for guiding video compression. Specifically, Hybrid Bidirectional Bimodal Attention (HBBA) enables bidirectional interactions between visual and semantic features during encoding and decoding. Semantic-Conditioned Cross-Attention (SCCA) incorporates semantic features into probability modeling during entropy coding. These semantic features provide high-level guidance throughout the pipeline, improving representation quality and encouraging semantic consistency through a transmitted text side channel. Experiments on UVG, MCL-JCV, and HEVC show that LLMVC consistently improves compression performance over traditional and recent neural video compression methods in terms of LPIPS and DISTS, while also achieving better fidelity than recent perceptual codecs.
articles.title_zh: LLMVC: 大型语言模型- Guided Generative 视频压缩

articles.title: VivaWorld: Long-Horizon Video World Model With Compositional 3D Priors
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33591v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon video generation is key to interactive world modeling, physical intelligence, and spatial reasoning, yet maintaining geometric consistency and accurate camera control remains challenging without 3D grounding. We introduce \textbf{VivaWorld}, a framework for generating geometry- and view-consistent long videos from an image. We first construct a compositional hybrid 3D representation that combines reconstructed point clouds, which preserve observed scene geometry and appearance, with generated textured meshes, which provide complete object geometry across $360^\circ$ novel views. We also introduce a connected-region filter removing inconsistent floating components for robust cross-view reconstruction and propose a hybrid camera embedding that combines global and object-anchored Pl\"{u}cker rays to capture both scene-level camera motion and camera-object relationships, and inject it together with the visual guidance into a video generation model via a control adapter. Extensive experiments show VivaWorld achieves state-of-the-art visual quality and camera control, while supporting controllable novel-view synthesis, long-horizon scene exploration, and physical AI. Project page is available at: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/sil/projects/vivaworld/
articles.title_zh: VivaWorld:长视视频世界模式与组成3D前传

articles.title: CariesBench: A Hierarchical Multi-view Benchmark for Dental Caries Screening and Diagnostic Reasoning from 3D Intraoral Scans
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dental caries assessment is a structured clinical process requiring lesion localization, identification of the affected tooth and surface, and severity grading rather than simple image-level recognition. 3D intraoral scans (IOS) preserve detailed dental geometry and surface morphology and support standardized rendering from complementary viewpoints, enabling fine-grained visual assessment while introducing a distinct need for anatomically grounded multi-view reasoning. Despite recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) and dental vision-language benchmarks, existing evaluations do not jointly assess hierarchical arch-to-tooth-to-surface reasoning, cross-view evidence integration, and surface-level caries assessment. To address this gap, we introduce CariesBench, a hierarchical benchmark constructed from 5,932 3D IOS, comprising 85,455 standardized multi-view renderings and 133,994 clinically grounded visual question answering instances with expert quality control. CariesBench comprises three complementary task families: Arch-level Clinical Screening (ACS), Tooth-level Diagnostic Reasoning (TDR), and Structured Clinical Decision-Making (SCD). Using the CariesBench training set, we further fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct to obtain IntraoralGPT. Extensive evaluation of 24 representative baseline MLLMs reveals a substantial benchmark-level performance disparity between arch-level screening and tooth-level diagnostic reasoning, with higher accuracy on ACS than on TDR. CariesBench-specific supervision substantially improves the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct baseline, increasing the 19-task macro-average clinical accuracy from 52.7% to 69.5% and TDR Overall from 34.4% to 44.7%.
articles.title_zh: Carys Bench:从3D内侧扫描中检测和诊断牙科疾病的分级多视图基准

articles.title: Linear-Time Online Visual Geometry Transformer with Hybrid Architecture
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformer-based 3D reconstruction models such as VGGT and $\pi^3$ predict cameras, depth and point maps directly from many input views. Causal attention models such as StreamVGGT extend them to online video but cache all past tokens, so their total compute grows quadratically with the stream length. Recurrent models such as CUT3R and TTT3R keep a fixed-size state at constant cost, but they progressively forget early geometry. We present LinearVGGT, a hybrid model distilled from StreamVGGT, which uses Mamba2 layers for efficient sequence modeling in three of every four global layers. The remaining layers use register-guided sparse attention to retrieve a few relevant past frames, compensating for the limited exact long-range recall of Mamba2. Our distillation needs only 9\% of the GPU hours and 31\% of the training frames that StreamVGGT uses to learn from VGGT. LinearVGGT keeps an almost constant latency of 27 ms per frame over 1,024 frames and is on average $12 \times$ faster than StreamVGGT. It outperforms its teacher and is competitive with the state-of-the-art streaming model LingBot-Map, while running $2.5\times$ faster and using $2.7\times$ less memory.
articles.title_zh: 带有混合结构的线性- 时空在线视觉几何变形器

articles.title: Look at What Matters: Learning Lesion Prototypes from Severity Labels for Domain-Generalized Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning models for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading often generalize poorly to unseen imaging domains, in part because predictions may exploit correlations specific to source datasets rather than retinal pathology. We address this challenge by constructing grading decisions from lesion evidence learned using only image severity labels. Clinical implications of DR grades provide multiple instance constraints that guide competitive learning of lesion and background prototypes at multiple scales. An additive ordinal scoring model then predicts severity exclusively from individual lesion prototype responses, explicitly connecting learned evidence with grading decisions without a global feature classification pathway. To improve the reliability of this evidence, we introduce teacher guided preservation under image degradations and spatial regularization against persistent coordinate preferences. Across six public DR datasets under a leave one domain out protocol, our method attains a mean quadratic weighted kappa of 0.761, outperforming the strongest competing method by 0.036. Localization and prototype removal analyses show that the learned responses align with retinal lesions and contribute to grading decisions. Experiments across five other prototype architectures and under image degradations further demonstrate the generality and robustness of the approach.
articles.title_zh: 看看什么重要:从Severity标签中学习Lesion原型,用于域域通用糖尿病肾上腺增生

articles.title: WorldUAV: Scaling UAV Data Synthesis via World Models
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: UAV detection and tracking remain constrained by the scarcity of high-quality training data. Existing game-engine-based synthetic UAV data suffer from a substantial synthetic-to-real gap, while the high cost of manually collected real-world UAV data limits dataset scale. Therefore, we introduce WorldUAV, a high-quality UAV dataset constructed through an efficient framework powered by world models. Specifically, WorldUAV directly integrates UAVs into readily available real-world videos, naturally preserving realistic backgrounds, illumination, and scene dynamics. Leveraging the spatiotemporal priors of world models, it generates UAV videos with plausible motion, pose variations, and cross-frame consistency, effectively narrowing the gap between synthetic and real data. We further develop an agentic pipeline orchestrated by a multimodal large language model that acquires sources, plans UAV trajectories, invokes synthesis, and verifies generated videos, enabling fully automated dataset construction. WorldUAV comprises 6,878 UAV videos and 205,778 UAV images. Experiments show that WorldUAV significantly improves the performance of UAV detectors. Moreover, it substantially reduces dataset construction costs, requiring only 15 seconds and USD 0.0005 API cost per high-quality UAV image. Our work offers both a high-quality dataset and a scalable data generation paradigm for UAV detection and tracking.
articles.title_zh: 世界无人驾驶飞行器:通过世界模型放大无人驾驶飞行器数据合成

articles.title: Efficient Scene-Distribution-Aware Second-Order Optimization for 3D Gaussian Splatting
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.33698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) optimization updates the Gaussian parameters one training view at a time, tens of thousands of times. Unlike such single-view updates, multi-view batches reduce dependence on individual training views, and second-order optimization reduces the number of updates with larger, structured parameter changes. Because fewer updates leave fewer chances to correct a change that fits only the views used in one update, scene coverage becomes more important for each second-order update. Multi-view second-order updates, however, are expensive. Pixel sampling reduces this cost, but two issues remain. First, selecting views without considering overlap leaves some views redundant. To address this, we propose a view selection strategy that reduces this redundancy. Second, existing work processes the sampled pixels of each view in a separate pass and recomputes alpha compositing for these pixels from scratch.
